sentences.zh: 皇甫謐

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Huangfu Mi.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐，字士安，幼名靜，安定朝那人，漢太尉嵩之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi, courtesy name Shi'an, childhood name Jing, was a man of Chaona in Anding commandery, and a great-grandson of Song, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi, whose courtesy name was Shi'an and childhood name Jing, came from Chaona in Anding; he was the great-grandson of Huangfu Song, who had served the Han as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 出叔父，徙居新安。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to an uncle and moved his residence to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously transferred to his uncle's line and the family relocated to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 年二十，不好學，遊蕩無度，或以為癡。

translations.literal: At age twenty he did not care for study; he roamed idly without restraint, and some considered him dull-witted.
translations.idiomatic: By twenty he still scorned books, drifted without purpose, and people took him for a simpleton.

sentences.zh: 嘗得瓜果，輒進所叔母任氏。

translations.literal: When he obtained melons or fruit, he would always present them to his aunt by adoption, Lady Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had fruit, he would bring it first to his adoptive aunt, Lady Ren.

sentences.zh: 任氏曰：「《孝經》云：『三牲之養，猶為不孝。

translations.literal: Lady Ren said: "The Classic of Filial Piety states: 'Even the nourishing of parents with the three sacrificial animals may still count as unfilial.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ren told him: "The Classic of Filial Piety says that even serving one's parents the finest triple sacrifice can still fall short of true filial piety."

sentences.zh: 』汝今年餘二十，目不存教，心不入道，無以慰我。

translations.literal: ' You are now past twenty; your eyes do not fix on instruction, your mind does not enter the Way—there is no way for you to comfort me.
translations.idiomatic: You are already past twenty, yet you pay no heed to teaching and your heart is not in the Way; that gives me no comfort."

sentences.zh: 」因歎曰：「昔孟母三徙以成仁，曾父烹豕以存教，豈我居不卜鄰，教有所闕，何爾魯鈍之甚也！

translations.literal: " Thereupon she sighed and said: "In olden days Mother Meng moved three times to complete her son's humanity; Zengzi's father cooked a pig to preserve teaching—could it be that I did not choose good neighbors for my dwelling, that there was some lack in my instruction, and that you are therefore so exceptionally dull!
translations.idiomatic: She sighed and went on: "Meng Ke's mother moved house three times to shape his character; Zeng Shen's father kept his word over a pig to teach honesty. Have I failed to pick our neighbors, or failed you as a teacher, that you should be so stubbornly slow?"

sentences.zh: 修身篤學，自汝得之，于我何有！

translations.literal: Cultivating the person and applying oneself earnestly to learning—you obtain these for yourself; what have they to do with me!
translations.idiomatic: Moral self-cultivation and serious study are yours to earn—what credit would they bring me?"

sentences.zh: 」因對之流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she wept before him.
translations.idiomatic: With that she wept in front of him.

sentences.zh: 謐乃感激，就鄉人席坦受書，勤力不怠。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon was stirred; he went to his fellow townsman Xi Tan to receive instruction in the classics and labored diligently without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her words, he studied under his townsman Xi Tan and applied himself without letting up.

sentences.zh: 居貧，躬自稼穡，帶經而農，遂博綜典籍百家之言。

translations.literal: Living in poverty, he personally plowed and harvested, carrying the classics with him as he farmed, and in the end broadly mastered the texts of the canon and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as he was, he worked the fields himself, classics tucked in his belt, until he had mastered the standard works and the writings of every school.

sentences.zh: 沈靜寡欲，始有高尚之志，以著述為務，自號玄晏先生。

translations.literal: Calm and retiring with few desires, he began to harbor lofty aims, took writing and compilation as his occupation, and styled himself Master Xuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and detached from ambition, he turned to scholarship as his life's work and took the sobriquet Master Xuanyan ('Dark Tranquility').

sentences.zh: 著《禮樂》、《聖真》之論。

translations.literal: He composed treatises titled 'Rites and Music' and 'Sagehood and Authenticity.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote discourses on ritual and music and on sagehood and truth.

sentences.zh: 後得風痹疾，猶手不輟卷。

translations.literal: Later he contracted wind-numbness illness, yet still his hand did not lay aside his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he fell ill with arthritic numbness, he never set his books aside.

sentences.zh: 或勸謐修名廣交，謐以為「非聖人孰能兼存出處，居田里之中亦可以樂堯、舜之道，何必崇接世利，事官鞅掌，然後為名乎」。

translations.literal: Some urged Mi to cultivate reputation and broaden his associations; Mi considered that 'unless one is a sage, who can simultaneously preserve both withdrawal and emergence? Dwelling in field and village, one may still take joy in the Way of Yao and Shun—why must one exalt contact with worldly profit, busy oneself with official duties in confusion, and only then count as having a name?'
translations.idiomatic: When others pressed him to network and seek fame, he replied that only a sage could harmonize public service and reclusion; even in the countryside one could live Yao and Shun's ideal—there was no need to chase office and profit merely to be somebody.

sentences.zh: 作《玄守論》以答之，曰：

translations.literal: He composed 'On Abiding in Mystery' to answer them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his essay "On Abiding in Mystery" in reply, which begins:

sentences.zh: 遂不仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore never entered government service.

sentences.zh: 耽玩典籍，忘寢與食，時人謂之「書淫」。

translations.literal: He was addicted to and delighted in the classics, forgetting sleep and food; people of the time called him a 'book debauchee.'
translations.idiomatic: He lost himself in texts to the point of skipping meals and sleep, and his contemporaries nicknamed him a "book lecher."

sentences.zh: 或有箴其過篤，將損耗精神。

translations.literal: Some admonished him that he was too intense and would waste his vital spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned that such obsession would ruin his health.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣，況命之修短分定懸天乎！」

translations.literal: Mi said: 'In the morning hear the Way; in the evening die—acceptable! How much more when the length or brevity of life is apportioned and hangs fixed from Heaven!'
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If I could hear the truth in the morning, I could die content that evening—and lifespan is heaven's decision anyway."

sentences.zh: 叔父有子既冠，謐年四十喪所生後母，遂還本宗。

translations.literal: When his uncle had a son who had already capped, Mi, at age forty, mourned the death of his birth mother who had been stepmother, and thereupon returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once his uncle had an heir of age, and Mi turned forty, he buried the stepmother who had raised him and reverted to his natural father's line.

sentences.zh: 城陽太守梁柳，謐從姑子也，當之官，人勸謐餞之。

translations.literal: Liang Liu, governor of Chengyang, was the son of Mi's father's cousin; when he was about to go to his post, people urged Mi to hold a farewell feast for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Liu of Chengyang commandery—Mi's cousin once removed—was leaving for his appointment, and neighbors wanted Mi to host a send-off banquet.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「柳為布衣時過吾，吾送迎不出門，食不過鹽菜，貧者不以酒肉為禮。

translations.literal: Mi said: 'When Liu was a commoner visiting me, I did not go beyond my gate to see him off or welcome him, and our meals did not go beyond salted vegetables—the poor do not take wine and meat as ritual courtesy.'
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "When Liang Liu was still a commoner and called on me, I never stepped outside my door for him and we ate nothing finer than pickles—modest households do not toast one another with meat and wine."

sentences.zh: 今作郡而送之，是貴城陽太守而賤梁柳，豈中古人之道，是非吾心所安也。」

translations.literal: Now that he holds a commandery and I send him off in this way, this would esteem the governor of Chengyang and slight Liang Liu—it cannot hit the mark of the ancients' Way; this is not what my heart finds acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: To fuss over him now that he wears an official's sash would honor the title of governor while slighting the man Liang Liu himself—that is not how the old worthies behaved, and it would not sit right with me."

sentences.zh: 時魏郡召上計掾，舉孝廉；

translations.literal: At that time Wei commandery summoned him as clerk for the annual accounts and nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: Wei commandery appointed him accounts clerk and nominated him for the Filial and Incorrupt examination;

sentences.zh: 景元初，相國辟，皆不行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingyuan era, the prime minister summoned him; in each case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyuan the chief minister tried to hire him as well, but he refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 其後鄉親勸令應命，謐為《釋勸論》以通志焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter his fellow villagers urged him to answer the summons; Mi composed 'Disquisition Explaining Persuasion' to clarify his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors pressed him to accept office, he wrote his "Disquisition Explaining Persuasion" to spell out his resolve.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：其後武帝頻下詔敦逼不已，謐上疏自稱草莽臣曰：「臣以尪弊，迷於道趣，因疾抽簪，散發林阜，人綱不閑，鳥獸為群。

translations.literal: Its text says: Thereafter Emperor Wu repeatedly issued edicts pressing him urgently without cease; Mi submitted a memorial styling himself 'a rustic subject of the weeds and thickets,' saying: 'I am worn and feeble, lost as to the path I should pursue; on account of illness I cast aside my hairpin, let my hair hang loose among woods and hills, am unversed in human ties, and keep company with birds and beasts.'
translations.idiomatic: The piece opens by noting that Emperor Wu kept issuing stern summonses; Mi answered with a memorial calling himself a mere "weed-country" subject: worn down and unsure of his direction, he had thrown aside office for illness, let his hair stream in the hills, shunned society, and lived like the birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 陛下披榛采蘭，並收蒿艾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty clears the brush to gather orchids and at the same time gathers mugwort and wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty clears the thorns for orchids yet gathers humble mugwort as well.

sentences.zh: 是以皋陶振褐，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Therefore Gao Yao shook his coarse cloak and the unkind went far away.
translations.idiomatic: Thus like Gao Yao of old in plain robes, you drive the vicious away.

sentences.zh: 臣惟頑蒙，備食晉粟，猶識唐人擊壤之樂，宜赴京城，稱壽闕外。

translations.literal: I am only stubbornly ignorant; yet though I merely partake of Jin millet, I still recognize the joy of Tang men beating the earth with clods—I ought to hurry to the capital and wish long life outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and untrained, yet even while eating Jin grain I remember the innocent delight of the ancient earth-clod song—I ought to rush to the capital and present my blessings below your gate.

sentences.zh: 而小人無良，致災速禍，久嬰篤疾，軀半不仁，右腳偏小，十有九載。

translations.literal: But this petty man lacks goodness; he has brought disaster and hastened calamity; long afflicted by grave illness, half his body is numb, his right foot is shrunken—it has been nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this worthless body has invited sickness: for nineteen years I have suffered paralysis down one side and wasting of the right foot.

sentences.zh: 又服寒食藥，違錯節度，辛苦荼毒，於今七年。

translations.literal: Moreover I took cold-food powder medicine, violated and confused its regimen, and suffered bitter torment—now seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Cold-food elixirs, wrongly dosed, have tormented me without cease these seven years.

sentences.zh: 隆冬裸袒食冰，當暑煩悶，加以咳逆，或若溫虐，或類傷寒，浮氣流腫，四肢酸重。

translations.literal: In deep winter I strip bare and eat ice; in summer heat I am vexed and stifled; added to this coughing fits, sometimes like warm malaria, sometimes resembling cold damage—floating qi flows into swelling, my four limbs ache and feel heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter finds me naked and chewing ice; midsummer brings feverish oppression, coughing attacks that mimic malaria or typhoid, watery swelling, and leaden limbs.

sentences.zh: 於今困劣，救命呼噏，父兄見出，妻息長訣。

translations.literal: Now I am exhausted and weak, crying out for rescue with gasping breaths; fathers and elder brothers have turned their backs; wife and children must take long farewell.
translations.idiomatic: I am reduced to gasping for breath while kin abandon me and my wife and children prepare their final goodbyes.

sentences.zh: 仰迫天威，扶輿就道，所苦加焉，不任進路，委身待罪，伏枕歎息。

translations.literal: Looking up I am pressed by heavenly majesty; leaning on a carriage I take the road—the suffering increases upon me; I cannot bear to advance on the route; I cast myself aside awaiting punishment, lying on my pillow sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding to imperial pressure I would drag myself onto the road, yet the journey would only worsen my pain; I cannot travel—I throw myself on your mercy and sigh upon my pillow.

sentences.zh: 臣聞《韶》《衛》不並奏，《雅》《鄭》不兼禦，故郤子入周，禍延王叔；

translations.literal: I have heard that Shao and Wei are not performed together, Ya and Zheng are not driven together by reins—therefore when the Xi lord entered Zhou, calamity extended to Prince Shu;
translations.idiomatic: As Shao and Wei were never played together, nor courtly airs mixed with Zheng tunes, the Xi heir's entry into Zhou spelled doom even for royal uncles.

sentences.zh: 虞丘稱賢，樊姬掩口。

translations.literal: When Yuqiu was praised as worthy, Lady Fan covered her mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqiu was hailed as a sage minister, Lady Fan of Chu hid a smile behind her sleeve.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，禮不同器，況臣糠䵃，糅之彫胡？

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man—rite does not share the same vessel with them—how much more am I chaff and bran to be mixed with polished foxtail millet?
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners were never served from the same bowl; how much less fit am I, mere bran, to be tossed with polished grain?

sentences.zh: 庸夫錦衣，不稱其服也。

translations.literal: A common fellow in brocade robes does not match his garments.
translations.idiomatic: Silk on a dullard never sits right.

sentences.zh: 竊聞同命之士，咸以畢到，唯臣疾疢，抱釁床蓐，雖貪明時，懼斃命路隅。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that gentlemen sharing the same summons have all arrived to completion; only I, sickly and clutching fault upon mat and bedding—though I covet this enlightened age, fear expiring by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Others summoned with me have reported for duty; I alone lie sick on my couch—however much I cherish your reign, I would only collapse on the road.

sentences.zh: 設臣不疾，已遭堯、舜之世，執志箕山，猶當容之。

translations.literal: Suppose I were not ill: having encountered the age of Yao and Shun, yet holding firm my resolve on Mount Ji, they still ought to tolerate me.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I were well, in an age as benign as Yao and Shun's a recluse who clung to Mount Ji would still deserve indulgence.

sentences.zh: 臣聞上有明聖之主，下有輸實之臣；

translations.literal: I have heard that above there is an enlightened sage lord; below there are ministers who convey substance;
translations.idiomatic: Where the throne shines bright, ministers speak plain truth;

sentences.zh: 上有在寬之政，下有委情之人。

translations.literal: above there is governance that resides in lenience; below there are men who entrust their genuine feelings.
translations.idiomatic: where policy stays generous, subjects may lay bare their hearts.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下留神垂恕，更旌瑰俊，索隱于傅岩，收釣於渭濱，無令泥滓久濁清流。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty attend with mind and extend forgiveness; seek out further splendid talents; search out the hidden at Fu's cliff and gather the angler on the Wei bank—do not let mud and sediment long muddy the clear current.
translations.idiomatic: Please look kindly on my plea, seek worthies at Fu Rock and the Wei waters, and keep silt from fouling the clear stream of office.

sentences.zh: 」謐辭切言至，遂見聽許。

translations.literal: ' Mi's words were cutting and his expressions extreme; thereupon he was heard and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was urgent and heartfelt, and the throne granted his excuse.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又舉賢良方正，並不起。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was again nominated Worthy and Good and Upright and Irregular—all without rising.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was nominated again as Worthy and Upright but still refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 自表就帝借書，帝送一車書與之。

translations.literal: He personally memorialized asking to borrow books from the emperor; the emperor sent him a cartload of books.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the throne for library loans and received an entire cart of texts.

sentences.zh: 謐雖羸疾，而披閱不怠。

translations.literal: Although Mi was emaciated from illness, he read without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Frail as he was, he never tired of reading.

sentences.zh: 初服寒食散，而性與之忤，每委頓不倫，嘗悲恚，叩刃欲自殺，叔母諫之而止。

translations.literal: When he first took cold-food powder, his nature ran counter to it; each time he collapsed in disorder, once he was grief-stricken and angry, knocked a blade and wished to kill himself—his aunt by adoption remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cold-food elixirs disagreed with his constitution: fits left him half dead with rage; once he seized a blade to end his life until his aunt talked him down.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守蜀人文立，表以命士有贄為煩，請絕其禮幣，詔從之。

translations.literal: Wen Li of Shu, governor of Jiyin, memorialized that for mandated scholars having gifts was troublesome and requested to cut off their ritual silk offerings—the edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li, governor of Jiyin, petitioned to scrap presentation gifts for appointed scholars, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 謐聞而歎曰：「亡國之大夫不可與圖存，而以革歷代之制，其可乎！

translations.literal: Mi heard this and sighed, saying: 'The grand officers of a destroyed state cannot be plotted with for preservation—yet by this alter institutions handed down through dynasties—is it acceptable!'
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi sighed: "Ministers of a fallen regime are poor counselors—yet does that justify junking age-old courtesy gifts?"

sentences.zh: 夫『束帛戔戔』，《易》之明義，玄纁之贄，自古之舊也。

translations.literal: As for 'bundles of silk in abundance'—it is the clear meaning of the Changes; dark and light silk as gifts is an ancient usage.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes celebrates stacked silks; dark-red presents are an immemorial custom.

sentences.zh: 故孔子稱夙夜強學以待問，席上之珍以待聘。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius praised studying hard morning and night to await questioning; treasures on the mat to await employment.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius urged scholars to master learning day and night and keep their talents like treasures spread for a worthy summons.

sentences.zh: 士於是乎三揖乃進，明致之難也；

translations.literal: The gentleman on this account bows three times only then advances—clarifying that bringing him in is difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Three deferential bows before stepping forward showed how hard it was to earn an invitation;

sentences.zh: 一讓而退，明去之易也。

translations.literal: one yielding then withdrawing—clarifying that leaving is easy.
translations.idiomatic: one courteous refusal and withdrawal showed how easily honor could be declined.

sentences.zh: 若殷湯之于伊尹，文王之于太公，或身即莘野，或就載以歸，唯恐禮之不重，豈吝其煩費哉！

translations.literal: Like Tang of Yin toward Yi Yin, King Wen toward the Grand Duke—sometimes the body itself goes to the wilderness of Shen, sometimes one rides the carriage to return—only fearing that the rite is not heavy; how could they be stingy about the bother and expense!
translations.idiomatic: King Tang visited Yi Yin in the wilds; King Wen fetched the Grand Duke in his carriage—they strained every ritual courtesy and never grudged the cost.

sentences.zh: 且一禮不備，貞女恥之，況命士乎！

translations.literal: Moreover if one rite is not complete, a chaste woman is shamed by it—how much more a mandated scholar!
translations.idiomatic: A modest maiden blushes if any courtesy is omitted—how much more a sworn scholar!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Si, you cherish your sheep; I cherish the rite.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told Zigong: you fret over the sheep; I care about the ritual."

sentences.zh: 』棄之如何？

translations.literal: ' If one discards it—what of it?
translations.idiomatic: What happens when we throw such traditions away?"

sentences.zh: 政之失賢，於此乎在矣。」

translations.literal: The government's losing worthy men—herein does it lie.'
translations.idiomatic: This is how states lose their best men."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，又詔曰：「男子皇甫謐沈靜履素，守學好古，與流俗異趣，其以謐為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning, there was again an edict saying: 'The man Huangfu Mi is composed and plain in conduct, guards learning and loves antiquity, his temper differs from vulgar currents—appoint Mi as Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning another edict praised Mi's sobriety and scholarship and named him Palace Attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」謐固辭篤疾。

translations.literal: ' Mi firmly declined on account of grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded grave illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝初雖不奪其志，尋復發詔徵為議郎，又召補著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor at first though not wresting his intent, soon again issued an edict summoning him as Gentleman Consultant, and again summoned him to supplement as Editorial Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first respected his wishes but soon summoned him as Gentleman Consultant and Editorial Director.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉劉毅請為功曹，並不應。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi requested him as clerk of merit—together he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, the metropolitan inspector, wanted him as clerk of records—again he declined.

sentences.zh: 著論為葬送之制，名曰《篤終》，曰：而竟不仕。

translations.literal: He composed a treatise setting forth regulations for burial and sending-off, titled 'Steadfast at the End,' saying: yet in the end he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his "Steadfast to the End" on funeral practice; throughout, he never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子童靈、方回等遵其遺命。

translations.literal: His sons Tongling, Fang Hui, and others followed his testamentary commands.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Tongling and Fang Hui carried out his last wishes.

sentences.zh: 謐所著詩賦誄頌論難甚多，又撰《帝王世紀》、《年曆》、《高士》、《逸士》、《列女》等傳、《玄晏春秋》，並重於世。

translations.literal: The poems, fu, dirges, hymns, treatises, and disputations composed by Mi were extremely numerous; he also compiled 'Annals of Emperors and Kings,' 'Chronological Calendar,' biographies of 'High Gentlemen,' 'Reclusive Gentlemen,' 'Exemplary Women,' and 'Spring and Autumn of Xuanyan'—all alike esteemed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left a vast body of verse, fu, laments, hymns, essays, and debates, plus his Annals of Kings, calendars, collections on eminent and reclusive worthy men, exemplary women, and the Xuanyan chronicle—each widely influential.

sentences.zh: 門人摯虞、張軌、牛綜、席純，皆為晉名臣。

translations.literal: His disciples Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, and Xi Chun all became renowned ministers of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Among his pupils Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, and Xi Chun rose to distinction under the Jin.

translations.literal: The printed text inserts an equals sign at this point.
translations.idiomatic: The edition marks a section division here.

sentences.zh: 子方回

translations.literal: Son Fang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Hui.

sentences.zh: =方回少遵父操，兼有文才。

translations.literal: Fang Hui, in his youth, observed his father's conduct; he also possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hui followed his father's austere example from youth and showed literary gifts of his own.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，博士征，不起。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia, the erudite office summoned him; he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia opened he was called to the academy doctorate but would not go.

sentences.zh: 避亂荊州，閉戶閒居，未嘗入城府。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he went to Jingzhou, closed his doors and dwelt at leisure, never entering the commandery or prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He fled the turmoil to Jingzhou, kept to his home, and never set foot in the regional seat.

sentences.zh: 蠶而後衣，耕而後食，先人後己，尊賢愛物，南土人士咸崇敬之。

translations.literal: He clothed himself after silkworms, ate after plowing; he put others before himself, honored the worthy and cherished creatures—gentlemen of the southern lands all revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He spun before he dressed, tilled before he ate, put others first, honored talent and cherished life—southerners held him in universal esteem.

sentences.zh: 刺史陶侃禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Inspector Tao Kan treated him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Kan showed him exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 侃每造之，著素士服，望門輒下而進。

translations.literal: Whenever Kan went to visit him, he wore plain scholar's garb; seeing the gate he dismounted from his carriage and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tao Kan called, he dressed as a simple scholar, dismounted at the gate, and walked in.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣從弟暠代侃，遷侃為廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent his cousin Wang Hao to replace Kan and transferred Kan to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun posted his cousin Wang Hao to supplant Tao Kan and moved Kan south to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侃將詣敦，方回諫曰：「吾聞敵國滅，功臣亡。

translations.literal: When Kan was about to go to Wang Dun, Fang Hui remonstrated, saying: 'I have heard that when an enemy state is destroyed, the merit ministers perish.'
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan prepared to visit Wang Dun, Fang Hui warned: "They say when the rival realm falls, its champions are next."

sentences.zh: 足下新破杜弢，功莫與二，欲無危，其可得乎！

translations.literal: You have newly broken Du Tao; merit matches no second—desiring to have no danger—how can it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: You have just crushed Du Tao—no one rivals your fame—do you really expect to stay safe?"

sentences.zh: 」侃不從而行。

translations.literal: ' Kan did not follow and went.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ignored him and went anyway.

sentences.zh: 敦果欲殺侃，賴周訪獲免。

translations.literal: Dun indeed wished to kill Kan; he relied on Zhou Fang to obtain escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun nearly had him killed; only Zhou Fang's intervention saved him.

sentences.zh: 暠既至荊州，大失物情，百姓叛暠迎杜弢。

translations.literal: After Hao arrived in Jingzhou, he greatly lost the sentiment of things; commoners rebelled against Hao and welcomed Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Hao took Jingzhou he forfeited popular support; people rose against him and sided with Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 暠大行誅戮以立威，以方回為侃所敬，責其不來詣己，乃收而斬之。

translations.literal: Hao carried out great executions and slaughterings to establish awe; because Fang Hui was one whom Kan respected, he blamed him for not coming to visit himself—thereupon seized him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao tried to terrify the region with executions; resenting Fang Hui's prestige—Tao Kan still revered him—he arrested Hui for refusing a personal audience and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 荊土華夷，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Chinese and barbarians of Jing lands—there were none who did not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and tribal peoples across Jing mourned him.

sentences.zh: 摯虞

translations.literal: Zhi Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Zhi Yu.

sentences.zh: 摯虞，字仲洽，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, courtesy name Zhongqia, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, styled Zhongqia, came from Chang'an in the Jingzhao capital district.

sentences.zh: 父模，魏太僕卿。

translations.literal: His father Mo served Wei as Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi Mo had been Wei Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 虞少事皇甫謐，才學通博，著述不倦。

translations.literal: Yu in youth studied under Huangfu Mi; his talent and learning were comprehensive and broad; he wrote tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Huangfu Mi, mastered wide learning, and wrote indefatigably.

sentences.zh: 郡檄主簿。

translations.literal: The commandery drafted him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery drafted him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 虞嘗以死生有命，富貴在天。

translations.literal: Yu once held that death and life have their allotments, wealth and honor lie with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu held that life span and fate are fixed, rank and wealth heaven-sent.

sentences.zh: 天之所祐者義也，人之所助者信也。

translations.literal: What Heaven aids is righteousness; what men help is trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blesses those who live rightly; men rally to those who keep faith.

sentences.zh: 履信思順，所以延福，違此而行，所以速禍。

translations.literal: Walking trust and thinking compliance—by this one extends blessing; violating this and acting—by this one hastens calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity and prudence lengthen fortune; their opposite hastens disaster.

sentences.zh: 然道長世短，禍福舛錯，怵迫之徒，不知所守，蕩而積憤，或迷或放。

translations.literal: Yet the Way is long and the age short; blessing and calamity are crossed and confused; those driven by fear and pressure do not know what they guard; dissipated they accumulate resentment—some lost, some unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the path is long while life is brief; fortune and disaster tangle; anxious souls lose their bearings, drift, and stockpile resentment—some grow deluded, others reckless.

sentences.zh: 故借之以身，假之以事，先陳處世不遇之難，遂棄彝倫，輕舉遠遊，以極常人罔惑之情，而後引之以正，反之以義，推神明之應於視聽之表，崇否泰之運于智力之外，以明天任命之不可違，故作《思遊賦》。

translations.literal: Therefore he borrowed it with his person, lent it with affairs—first setting forth the hardship of not meeting one's time in dwelling in the world, thereupon abandoning constant norms, lightly rising and roaming far, to exhaust the feelings by which ordinary men are deluded and confused, and afterward leading them with rectitude, returning them with righteousness, inferring spirit illumination's responses beyond sight and hearing, exalting the turns of blockage and ease outside intelligence and strength, to clarify that Heaven-mandated destiny cannot be disobeyed—therefore he composed 'Fu on Pondering Roaming.'
translations.idiomatic: So he used his own story and imagined journeys—first sketching the bitterness of unappreciated scholars who abandon duty for restless travel, mapping ordinary confusion, then steering readers back toward righteousness, arguing that divine response lies beyond the senses and fortune beyond clever plans, all to show heaven's decree cannot be resisted; hence his "Rhapsody on Roaming Thought."

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：舉賢良，與夏侯湛等十七人策為下第，拜中郎。

translations.literal: Its text says: He was nominated Worthy and Good; with Xia Hou Zhan and seventeen others he was examined and ranked in the lower tier; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The source text runs together the fu preface with later events: nominated Worthy and Good, he placed lowest among eighteen candidates including Xia Hou Zhan and received an honorary Gentleman title.

sentences.zh: 武帝詔曰：「省諸賢良答策，雖所言殊塗，皆明于王義，有益政道。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict saying: 'I have examined the answer essays of the various Worthy and Good candidates; although what they say differs in road, all are illumined in kingly righteousness and beneficial to governance.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu observed that although each worthy's policy essay took a different tack, all clarified royal principle and served good government.

sentences.zh: 欲詳覽其對，究觀賢士大夫用心。

translations.literal: I desire to examine in detail their replies and exhaustively observe the intentions of worthy grand officers and gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to study every answer closely and weigh the minds of these scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 」因詔諸賢良方正直言，會東堂策問，曰：「頃日食正陽，水旱為災，將何所修，以變大眚？

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the various Worthy and Good, Upright and Straight-speaking candidates to assemble at the Eastern Hall for policy examination, saying: "Recently there was a solar eclipse at zheng-yang; floods and droughts became calamities—what shall we cultivate to transform this great mishap?
translations.idiomatic: He then convened the worthy candidates at the Eastern Hall and asked why recent eclipses and floods struck the heartland and what reform could avert such sweeping ill.

sentences.zh: 及法令有不宜於今，為公私所患苦者，皆何事？

translations.literal: As for statutes and ordinances unsuited to the present age that cause distress to both public and private interests—what are all these matters?
translations.idiomatic: Which laws today harm both state and subject alike?

sentences.zh: 凡平世在於得才，得才者亦借耳目以聽察。

translations.literal: In general, peace in an age lies in obtaining talent; those who obtain talent likewise borrow ears and eyes to listen and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Stable rule rests on finding the right men, and rulers must keep eyes and ears open.

sentences.zh: 若有文武器能有益於時務而未見申敘者，各舉其人。

translations.literal: If there are civil and martial talents that could aid current affairs yet have not been recommended and documented, each shall nominate such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who knows officials whose skills could serve the realm must put their names forward.

sentences.zh: 及有負俗謗議，宜先洗濯者，亦各言之。

translations.literal: And as for those burdened by vulgar slander who ought first to be cleared, each shall likewise speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone unjustly smeared who deserves rehabilitation should also be named.

sentences.zh: 」虞對曰：「臣聞古之聖明，原始以要終，體本以正末。

translations.literal: Yu replied, saying: "I have heard that sages of antiquity examined origins to grasp outcomes and embodied the root to rectify the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu answered that ancient sage-kings traced effects to causes and governed from principle outward.

sentences.zh: 故憂法度之不當，而不憂人物之失所；

translations.literal: Therefore they worried that laws and standards were inappropriate, not that men and affairs lost their stations;
translations.idiomatic: They worried first about bad law, not misplaced personnel;

sentences.zh: 憂人物之失所，而不憂災害之流行。

translations.literal: they worried that men and affairs lost their stations, not that disasters spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: then about mismatched appointments, not random natural catastrophes.

sentences.zh: 誠以法得於此，則物理於彼；

translations.literal: Truly because when law obtains here, natural principle is ordered there;
translations.idiomatic: When statutes align below, heaven's pattern rights itself above;

sentences.zh: 人和於下，則災消於上。

translations.literal: harmony among those below, then calamities dissolve above.
translations.idiomatic: harmony in the realm dissolves omens in the sky.

sentences.zh: 其有日月之眚，水旱之災，則反聽內視，求其所由，遠觀諸物，近驗諸身。

translations.literal: If there are blemishes of sun and moon, disasters of flood and drought, then turn listening inward and seek their causes; gaze far at myriad things, examine near upon one's person.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven sends eclipse or flood, a ruler searches policy and conscience alike.

sentences.zh: 耳目聽察，豈或有蔽其聰明者乎？

translations.literal: In listening with ears and inspecting with eyes—could anything obstruct clarity and brightness?
translations.idiomatic: Has anything dulled your ears or eyes?

sentences.zh: 動心出令，豈或有傾其常正者乎？

translations.literal: In stirring the mind and issuing orders—could anything overturn constant correctness?
translations.idiomatic: Have decrees strayed from steady principle?

sentences.zh: 大官大職，豈或有授非其人者乎？

translations.literal: In great offices and great posts—could anyone have been appointed who was not the right person?
translations.idiomatic: Have high posts gone to unworthy men?

sentences.zh: 賞罰黜陟，豈或有不得其所者乎？

translations.literal: In rewards, punishments, demotions, and promotions—could anyone have failed to obtain what was fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Have rewards and punishments missed their mark?

sentences.zh: 河濱山岩，豈或有懷道釣築而未感於夢兆者乎？

translations.literal: Along rivers and mountain cliffs—could anyone embracing the Way, fishing or building, have failed to stir dream-portents?
translations.idiomatic: Have recluses whose virtue should move heaven gone unnoticed?

sentences.zh: 方外遐裔，豈或有命世傑出而未蒙膏澤者乎？

translations.literal: Beyond the borders in distant corners—could anyone outstanding for the age have failed to receive enriching moisture?
translations.idiomatic: Have frontier talents lacked your nurturing rain?

sentences.zh: 推此類也，以求其故，詢事考言，以盡其實，則天人之情可得而見，咎征之至可得而救也。

translations.literal: Extend reasoning of this kind to seek its causes; inquire into affairs and examine words to exhaust substance—then dispositions of Heaven and men may be observed and arrivals of blameful omens may be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Ask such questions honestly and heaven's intent becomes legible; omens can then be answered with reform.

sentences.zh: 若推之於物則無忤，求之於身則無尤，萬物理順，內外咸宜，祝史正辭，言不負誠，而日月錯行，夭癘不戒，此則陰陽之事，非吉凶所在也。

translations.literal: If pushed against things there is no clash, sought in oneself there is no fault, myriad principles are ordered, inner and outer both fitting, invokers of blessing speak correct words without betraying sincerity—yet sun and moon run awry and epidemic pestilence gives no warning—then these are matters of yin and yang, not where auspiciousness and inauspiciousness reside.
translations.idiomatic: When government and conscience are sound yet odd skies persist, blame cosmic imbalance—not moral failure.

sentences.zh: 期運度數，自然之分，固非人事所能供禦，其亦振廩散滯，貶食省用而已矣。

translations.literal: Expected cycles and reckonings of fate are natural allotments—fundamentally not what human affairs can supply or control; one may only open granaries to relieve blockage, reduce food, and curtail expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar fate lies beyond men; all we can do is open granaries, tighten belts, and ease suffering.

sentences.zh: 是故誠遇期運，則雖陶唐、殷湯有所不變；

translations.literal: Therefore if one truly meets the destined period, even Tao Tang and Yin Tang could not change it;
translations.idiomatic: When heaven fixes a season of doom, even Yao and Tang could not shift it;

sentences.zh: 苟非期運，則宋、衛之君，諸侯之相，猶能有感。

translations.literal: if it is not the destined period, then even lords of Song and Wei and ministers among the feudal lords could still produce resonant effects.
translations.idiomatic: yet outside such doom minor sovereigns could still move heaven by virtue.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下審其所由，以盡其理，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine the grounds thereof and exhaust their principles—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Probe causes this thoroughly and the empire profits.

sentences.zh: 臣生長蓽門，不逮異物，雖有賢才，所未接識，不敢瞽言妄舉，無以疇答聖問。

translations.literal: I was raised in a humble gate and have not encountered unusual persons; though worthy men exist, I have not met or known them—I dare not speak blindly or nominate rashly and have no means to answer Your sagely question.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in obscurity, I know too few men to recommend anyone worthy of your question.

sentences.zh: 」擢為太子舍人，除聞喜令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Gentleman of the Heir Apparent and appointed magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to crown prince's gentleman and magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 時天子留心政道，又吳寇新平，天下乂安，上《太康頌》以美晉德。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven devoted mind to government ways; moreover the Wu foe had newly been pacified and the realm was peaceful—he presented "The Taikang Ode" to praise Jin virtue.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor focused on good rule and Wu had just surrendered, he offered his Taikang ode praising the Jin.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: The ode begins:

sentences.zh: :於休上古，人之資始。

translations.literal: How splendid was high antiquity—the beginning that endowed mankind.
translations.idiomatic: Glory to deepest antiquity—source of every blessing.

sentences.zh: 四隩咸宅，萬國同軌。

translations.literal: The four marches all dwell; myriad states share one track.
translations.idiomatic: All quarters settled; every kingdom rode one axle-track.

sentences.zh: 有漢不競，喪亂靡紀。

translations.literal: Han lost its competitiveness; turmoil lost all norm.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han faltered; chaos erased every statute.

sentences.zh: 畿服外叛，侯衛內圮。

translations.literal: The royal domain rebelled without; guards collapsed within.
translations.idiomatic: Heartlands rose in revolt; palace guards crumbled within.

sentences.zh: 天難既降，時惟鞠凶。

translations.literal: Heaven's hardship having descended, the hours knew only crushing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's scourge arrived; the age reeked of cruelty.

sentences.zh: 龍戰獸爭，分裂遐邦。

translations.literal: Dragons battled and beasts strove; distant regions split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords tore the provinces like beasts at war.

sentences.zh: 備僭岷蜀，度逆海東。

translations.literal: Bei presumptuously seized Min and Shu; Du crossed to the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei seized Shu beyond Min; enemies sailed the eastern sea.

sentences.zh: 權乃緣間，割據三江。

translations.literal: Sun Quan then exploited the breach and carved out the three rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan exploited the breach and held the Yangzi triple fork.

sentences.zh: 明明上帝，臨下有赫。

translations.literal: Bright August Heaven above looks down with awesome power.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven glares from above.

sentences.zh: 乃宣皇威，致天之辟。

translations.literal: Then the martial sovereign spread awe and executed Heaven's punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Our martial emperor wielded awe and heaven's sentence.

sentences.zh: 奮武遼隧，罪人斯獲。

translations.literal: His might was roused at Liaosui; the guilty were captured.
translations.idiomatic: His hosts thundered along Liaosui and seized the guilty.

sentences.zh: 撫定朝鮮，奄征韓、貊。

translations.literal: He pacified Joseon and campaigned to Han and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He settled Korea and marched against Han and Mo.

sentences.zh: 文既應期，席捲梁、益。

translations.literal: When culture answered the hour, he swept Liang and Yi like rolling up a mat.
translations.idiomatic: When civil virtue matched the hour, Liang and Yi rolled up like mats.

sentences.zh: 元憝委命，九夷重譯。

translations.literal: The chief villain surrendered his fate; the nine Yi arrived through successive interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: The arch rebel yielded his mandate; nine Yi peoples reached court through relay interpreters.

sentences.zh: 邛、冉、哀牢，是焉底績。

translations.literal: Qiong, Ran, and Ailao—there he laid his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern Qiong, Ran, and Ailao bowed to his achievement.

sentences.zh: 我皇之登，二國既平。

translations.literal: When Our Emperor ascended, those two states were already pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When our emperor mounted the throne, both rival realms had fallen.

sentences.zh: 靡適不懷，以育群生。

translations.literal: None who stayed away failed to cherish him; he nurtured the masses.
translations.idiomatic: None beyond reach refused him; he fed every life.

sentences.zh: 吳乃負固，放命南冥。

translations.literal: Wu then relied on terrain and defied command in the southern deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wu still hugged its rivers and flouted edicts in the southern dark.

sentences.zh: 聲教未暨，弗及王靈。

translations.literal: Sound and instruction had not reached them; kingly numinous power did not extend.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing teaching had not touched them; royal majesty stalled.

sentences.zh: 皇震其威，赫如雷霆。

translations.literal: The sovereign shook his might—awe like thunderclap.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath crashed like thunder.

sentences.zh: 截彼江、沔，荊、舒以清。

translations.literal: He cut through Jiang and Han; Jing and Shu were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He severed Jiang and Han until Jing and Shu ran clear.

sentences.zh: 邈矣聖皇，參乾兩離。

translations.literal: Far-flung is the sage sovereign—paired with Qian, twin Li.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty the sage king—spanning heaven's pivot like paired trigrams.

sentences.zh: 陶化以正，取亂以奇。

translations.literal: He molded transformation with rectitude; seized chaos with surprise.
translations.idiomatic: He shaped order through candor and seized chaos by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 耀武六旬，輿徒不疲。

translations.literal: For sixty days he displayed arms—yet carriers never tired.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty days of campaigning wearied neither wagons nor men.

sentences.zh: 飲至數實，幹旄無虧。

translations.literal: They drank at return and counted rewards—royal banners unfurled without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Victory wine flowed; banners flew spotless.

sentences.zh: 洋洋四海，率禮和樂。

translations.literal: Vast is the four seas—all observe rites and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Across four seas all tread ritual and song.

sentences.zh: 穆穆宮廟，歌雍詠鑠。

translations.literal: Solemn the palace shrines—they sing Yong and chant splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Temples echo with hymns of praise.

sentences.zh: 光天之下，莫匪帝略。

translations.literal: Beneath heaven's effulgence none escape the emperor's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Under radiant heaven none escape his design.

sentences.zh: 窮發反景，承正受朔。

translations.literal: Even farthest barbarians and sunset realms receive orthodox calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Even distant tribes facing polar gloom accept his calendar.

sentences.zh: 龍馬騤騤，風于華陽。

translations.literal: Dragon-horses prance; winds breathe at Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-steeds stamp; winds sigh along Huayang.

sentences.zh: 弓矢橐服，干戈戢藏。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows in quiver-sleeves; shields and spears stored away.
translations.idiomatic: Bows rest in cases; shields and spears gather dust.

sentences.zh: 嚴嚴南金，業業餘皇。

translations.literal: Stern southern metal—towering war-galleys.
translations.idiomatic: Southern bells ring from towering fleets.

sentences.zh: 雄劍班朝，造舟為梁。

translations.literal: Hero blades ranked at court; built boats bridge the stream.
translations.idiomatic: Keen swords line the hall; pontoon bridges span the waves.

sentences.zh: 聖明有造，實代天工。

translations.literal: The sage's brilliance creates—truly replacing Heaven's craft.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's creation rivals heaven's workmanship.

sentences.zh: 天地不違，黎元時邕。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth do not oppose him; the black-haired folk prosper in season.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth assent; commoners thrive in step.

sentences.zh: 三務斯協，用底厥庸。

translations.literal: The three tasks harmonize—thus his merit is brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The three prime duties align; his merit closes perfect.

sentences.zh: 既遠其跡，將明其蹤。

translations.literal: Already remote his traces—soon plain his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: His footprints fade yet blaze plain on stone.

sentences.zh: 喬山惟嶽，望帝之封。

translations.literal: Lofty Mount Qiao—Emperor Shun's fief mound.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Qiao towers—mark of Emperor Shun's mound.

sentences.zh: 猗歟聖帝，胡不封哉！

translations.literal: Oh sage emperor—why was he not enfeoffed!
translations.idiomatic: O sage liege—why withhold your mound!

sentences.zh: 以母憂解職。

translations.literal: He resigned office mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，召補尚書郎。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was summoned to supplement as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Much later he returned as a secretary at the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠陳勰掘地得古尺，尚書奏：「今尺長於古尺，宜以古為正。

translations.literal: Chief Architect Chen Xie dug earth and obtained an ancient foot-rule; the Masters of Writing memorialized: "Today's rule is longer than the ancient—we ought to take the ancient as correct."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xie unearthed an old measuring rod, the ministry argued today's chi ran long and urged restoring the antique standard.

sentences.zh: 」潘嶽以為慣用已久，不宜復改。

translations.literal: Pan Yue held that habit had long used the present measure and it was unsuitable to change again.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue protested that generations had used the longer chi.

sentences.zh: 虞駁曰：「昔聖人有以見天下之賾而擬其形容，象物制器，以存時用。

translations.literal: Yu refuted, saying: "Ancient sages who saw the profundity of the realm modeled forms after things and fashioned implements to preserve timely use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu countered that sages modeled tools on nature to serve daily needs.

sentences.zh: 故參天兩地，以正算數之紀；

translations.literal: Therefore they matched heaven triply and earth doubly to rectify reckoning of calculations;
translations.idiomatic: They paired heaven's three lights with earth's two forces to anchor mathematics;

sentences.zh: 依律計分，以定長短之度。

translations.literal: they relied on pitch pipes to compute fractions to settle measures of length.
translations.idiomatic: they tied length to pitch-pipe fractions.

sentences.zh: 其作之也有則，故用之也有征。

translations.literal: Their making had patterns; therefore their application had verification.
translations.idiomatic: Design followed rule, so use matched proof.

sentences.zh: 考步兩儀，則天地無所隱其情；

translations.literal: Examining the two luminaries in step—Heaven and Earth cannot hide disposition;
translations.idiomatic: Align sun and moon and heaven hides nothing;

sentences.zh: 准正三辰，則懸象無所容其謬；

translations.literal: aligning and correcting the three celestial markers—suspended phenomena cannot harbor error;
translations.idiomatic: true the three celestial markers and stars cannot lie;

sentences.zh: 施之金石，則音韻和諧；

translations.literal: applied to metal and stone—tones and resonance harmonize;
translations.idiomatic: strike bells and stones and pitch locks;

sentences.zh: 措之規矩，則器用合宜。

translations.literal: laid on compass and square—vessels and tools fit use.
translations.idiomatic: lay compass and square and every vessel fits.

sentences.zh: 一本不差而萬物皆正，及其差也，事皆反是。

translations.literal: One root without discrepancy and myriad things are correct; when discrepancy arises, affairs reverse this.
translations.idiomatic: One true gauge orders all; error inverts everything.

sentences.zh: 今尺長於古尺幾於半寸，樂府用之，律呂不合；

translations.literal: Now the present rule exceeds the ancient by nearly half an inch; when the Music Bureau uses it, pitch pipes do not match;
translations.idiomatic: Today's chi overshoots the old by half an inch—music falls out of tune;

sentences.zh: 史官用之，曆象失占；

translations.literal: when clerks of history use it, celestial patterns lose prognostications;
translations.idiomatic: historians lose celestial forecasts;

sentences.zh: 醫署用之，孔穴乖錯。

translations.literal: when the medical office uses it, acupuncture points go awry.
translations.idiomatic: physicians miss every point.

sentences.zh: 此三者，度量之所由生，得失之所取征，皆絓閡而不得通，故宜改今而從古也。

translations.literal: These three are what measures stem from and where gain and loss take verification—all are tangled and obstructed and cannot communicate—therefore it is fitting to change the present and follow the ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Music, calendar, and medicine all ride on measure—each now jams—so we must revert to the ancient chi.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之制，同律度量衡，仲尼之訓，謹權審度。

translations.literal: Institutions of Tang and Yu unified pitch pipes, measures, weights, and balances; Confucius's teaching was careful with weights and examined measures.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun unified pitch, length, volume, and weight; Confucius urged careful scales.

sentences.zh: 今兩尺並用，不可謂之同；

translations.literal: Now two rules are used together—it cannot be called unified;
translations.idiomatic: Two rulers at once cannot mean unity;

sentences.zh: 知失而行，不可謂之謹。

translations.literal: knowing the error yet proceeding—it cannot be called careful.
translations.idiomatic: knowing error yet marching on is not caution;

sentences.zh: 不同不謹，是謂謬法，非所以軌物垂則，示人之極。

translations.literal: Neither unified nor careful—this is called mistaken law; it is not how to regulate things, hand down norms, or show people utmost standards.
translations.idiomatic: Neither unified nor careful is false law—no model for the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡物有多而易改，亦有少而難變，亦有改而致煩，有變而之簡。

translations.literal: Among things some are many and easy to alter, some few and hard to change; some alterations bring trouble, some changes lead to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Some reforms stir trouble; others simplify.

sentences.zh: 度量是人所常用，而長短非人所戀惜，是多而易改者也。

translations.literal: Measures are what people constantly use, yet lengths are not what people cling to—these are many and easy to alter.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone uses yardsticks daily yet hardly fetishizes a chi—easy to fix.

sentences.zh: 正失於得，反邪于正，一時之變，永世無二，是變而之簡者也。

translations.literal: Correcting loss into gain, returning deviation to rectitude—a single generation's change, none different for ages—is change tending toward simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Righting wrong measures once sets generations straight—that is simple reform.

sentences.zh: 憲章成式，不失舊物，季末苟合之制，異端雜亂之用，當以時厘改，貞夫一者也。

translations.literal: Statutes following established patterns without losing old objects—expedient compromises of late decadence and miscellaneous usages from heterodox schools ought to be rectified in due course toward unity.
translations.idiomatic: Guard true precedent; sweep away Late Han shortcuts and odd usages until only one measure remains.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜如所奏。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it fitting to follow the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He urged adopting the ministry's memorial.

sentences.zh: 」又表論封禪，見《禮志》。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on feng and shan sacrifices—see the "Treatise on Rites."
translations.idiomatic: His essay on the Feng and Shan rites appears in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 虞以漢末喪亂，譜傳多亡失，雖其子孫不能言其先祖，撰《族姓昭穆》十卷，上疏進之，以為足以備物致用，廣多聞之益。

translations.literal: Yu, because at Han's end turmoil caused genealogies largely to perish—even descendants could not name remote ancestors—compiled "Clans and Surnames: Seniority Grades" in ten rolls and submitted it, deeming it sufficient to prepare objects for use and broaden benefit of wide learning.
translations.idiomatic: After Han chaos erased clan registers, he compiled ten fascicles on surname ranks so scholars could recover lineage.

sentences.zh: 以定品違法，為司徒所劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: For violating regulations in fixing ranks he was impeached by the Minister of Education; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of education impeached him for irregular promotions; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 時太廟初建，詔普增位一等。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Temple was first erected; an edict universally raised rank one degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial temple opened, an edict promoted every official one rank.

sentences.zh: 後以主者承詔失旨，改除之。

translations.literal: Later because the responsible official carried out the edict contrary to intent, the promotion was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats botched the order and the bonus rank was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 虞上表曰：「臣聞昔之聖明，不愛千乘之國而惜桐葉之信，所以重至尊之命而達于萬國之誠也。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that sages of old did not spare a state of a thousand chariots yet treasured faith like the Tong-leaf tale—thereby honoring supreme commands and conveying sincerity to myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that worthies prized a leaf's promise over a kingdom—edicts must stay trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 前《乙巳赦書》，遠稱先帝遺惠餘澤，普增位一等，以酬四海欣戴之心。

translations.literal: The former Yisi amnesty edict far praised the late emperor's lingering grace and residual moisture and universally raised rank one degree to repay hearts of the four seas who rejoiced and bore allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The prior Yisi edict credited the late emperor's grace and raised every rank to reward loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 驛書班下，被於遠近，莫不鳥騰魚躍，喜蒙德澤。

translations.literal: Dispatches were posted far and near—none did not leap like birds or fish, rejoicing to receive virtue's moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Courier notices raced everywhere; subjects danced like fish and birds under fresh rain.

sentences.zh: 今一旦更以主者思文不審，收既往之詔，奪已澍之施，臣之愚心竊以為不可。

translations.literal: Now once because the responsible official reflected on the text without care, they withdrew an edict already issued and seized favors already poured forth—in my foolish heart I privately deem this impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: To revoke a published decree because clerks misread the wording betrays every pledge already granted.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ' An edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his protest.

sentences.zh: 元康中，遷吳王友。

translations.literal: During Yuankang he was transferred to be Companion to the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang he became companion to the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗撰《新禮》，使虞討論得失而後施行。

translations.literal: At that time Xun Yi compiled the New Rites and had Yu debate gains and losses before implementing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi drafted new ritual statutes and had Zhi Yu vet them before promulgation.

sentences.zh: 元皇后崩，杜預奏：「諒暗之制，乃自上古，是以高宗無服喪之文，而唯文稱不言。

translations.literal: When Empress Yuan died, Du Yu memorialized: "The curtained-mourning institution stems from high antiquity—thus Gaozong has no text on wearing mourning; documents speak only of holding silence."
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Yuan died, Du Yu cited classical silent mourning and noted Emperor Wu Ding was remembered only for holding silence, not garment schedules.

sentences.zh: 漢文限三十六日。

translations.literal: Han Wendi limited it to thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi capped mourning at thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 魏氏以降，既虞為節。

translations.literal: From Wei onward, completion of the Yu sacrifice became the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei, mourning ended after the Yu sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皇太子與國為體，理宜釋服，卒哭便除。

translations.literal: The crown prince shares substance with the state—by principle he ought to set aside mourning garments and remove them at the end of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent embodies the state—he should shed mourning once the weeping rites conclude.

sentences.zh: 」虞答預書曰：「唐稱遏密，殷雲諒暗，各舉事以為名，非既葬有殊降。

translations.literal: Yu answered Du Yu's letter, saying: "Tang spoke of halting music; Yin spoke of curtained mourning—each cited an affair for its name; it is not that after burial there was some separate reduction."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu replied that Tang's silenced instruments and Yin's dark chamber were slogans, not extra reductions after burial.

sentences.zh: 周室以來，謂之喪服。

translations.literal: Since Zhou times it has been called mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou people simply called these mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 喪服者，以服表喪。

translations.literal: Mourning dress means using garments to display mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress visibly signals grief.

sentences.zh: 今帝者一日萬機，太子監撫之重，以宜奪禮，葬訖除服，變制通理，垂典將來，何必附之于古，使老儒致爭哉！

translations.literal: Now the emperor manages myriad affairs in a day; the heir's oversight duty is weighty—therefore it is fitting to curtail rites, remove garments after burial, alter regulations to accord with principle, hand down canons to posterity—why cling to antiquity and make old scholars quarrel!
translations.idiomatic: Throne and heir face crushing burdens—trimming ritual after burial suits common sense better than letting pedants brawl over precedent.

sentences.zh: 」皇太孫尚薨，有司奏「御服齊衰期」。

translations.literal: When imperial grandson Shang died, the relevant office memorialized "the sovereign's garments zicui for one full year."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial grandson died, officials prescribed the emperor's one-year zicui mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔令博士議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the erudites to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered academic officials to debate it.

sentences.zh: 虞曰：「太子生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Yu said: "When the heir was born, he was raised with adult rites—therefore child-death logic is removed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued the imperial grandson had been invested with adult rites—infant-mortuary rules no longer applied.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服全，非以年也。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson likewise embodies the lord's transmission of weight—through position being complete his garments are complete, not through age.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson bore succession duty—his mourning matched rank, not calendar age.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ' They followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 虞又議玉輅、兩社事，見《輿服志》。

translations.literal: Yu also deliberated the jade chariot and the two altars of soil—see the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials on the jade carriage and paired soil altars appear in the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.

sentences.zh: 後曆秘書監、衛尉卿，從惠帝幸長安。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of the Guards, following Emperor Hui to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later directed the imperial library and commanded the guards, accompanying Emperor Hui west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及東軍來迎，百官奔散，遂流離鄠、杜之間，轉入南山中，糧絕饑甚，拾橡實而食之。

translations.literal: When eastern armies came to welcome them, the hundred officials fled in disorder; he drifted destitute between Hu and Du, then turned into the southern hills—food cut off, terribly hungry, he gathered oak fruits and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern relief arrived the court scattered; he wandered between Hu and Du and fled into the Zhongnan hills, starving until he gathered acorns to eat.

sentences.zh: 後得還洛，曆光祿勳、太常卿。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return to Luoyang and successively served as Supervisor of the Household and Minister of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually reached Luoyang as chamberlain for the imperial household and minister of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時懷帝親郊。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Huai personally sacrificed at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai personally performed the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自元康以來，不親郊祀，禮儀弛廢。

translations.literal: Since Yuankang, he had not personally attended suburban sacrifice—rites grew lax and fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuankang no emperor had personally worshipped heaven—outer ritual had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 虞考正舊典，法物粲然。

translations.literal: Yu collated old canons—implements and regalia shone complete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu restored the old liturgy so vessels and banners gleamed in proper array.

sentences.zh: 及洛京荒亂，盜竊縱橫，人饑相食。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell to chaos, theft ran rampant and starving people ate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's collapse unleashed thieves and cannibal famine.

sentences.zh: 虞素清貧，遂以餒卒。

translations.literal: Yu had always been poor and clean—thereupon he starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Always poor and honest, he died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 虞撰《文章志》四卷，注解《三輔決錄》，又撰古文章，類聚區分為三十卷，名曰《流別集》，各為之論，辭理愜當，為世所重。

translations.literal: Yu compiled Records of Literary Works in four rolls, annotated Judgments on the Three Auxiliaries, also compiled ancient compositions classified into thirty rolls titled Collected Genres, each with commentary—phrasing and reasoning apt, esteemed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left a four-scroll literary gazetteer, glosses on the Sanfu judgments, and thirty fascicles of categorized ancient prose called Collected Genres with critical essays—widely admired.

sentences.zh: 虞善觀玄象，嘗謂友人曰：「今天下方亂，避難之國，其唯涼土乎！

translations.literal: Yu was skilled at observing celestial signs; once he told a friend: "The realm will soon be in chaos—the land that offers refuge can only be Liangzhou!"
translations.idiomatic: Reading the sky he told friends only Liangzhou would shelter fugitives from coming turmoil.

sentences.zh: 」性愛士人，有表薦者，恆為其辭。

translations.literal: ' By nature he cherished scholars; whenever someone submitted a memorial of recommendation he always drafted the wording for them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved nurturing scholars and habitually ghost-wrote recommendations.

sentences.zh: 東平太叔廣樞機清辯，廣談，虞不能對；

translations.literal: Taishu Guang of Dongping was acute and eloquent in debate; when Guang conversed at length Yu could not reply;
translations.idiomatic: Taishu Guang of Dongping sparkled in oral debate—Zhi Yu could not match him live;

sentences.zh: 虞筆，廣不能答；

translations.literal: when Yu wrote, Guang could not answer;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhi Yu wrote, Guang could not respond;

sentences.zh: 更相嗤笑，紛然於世雲。

translations.literal: They sneered at each other by turns—through the capital rumor ran confused.
translations.idiomatic: They traded barbs until Luoyang buzzed with gossip.

sentences.zh: 束晳

translations.literal: Shu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Shu Xi.

sentences.zh: 束晳，字廣微，陽平元城人，漢太子太傅疏廣之後也。

translations.literal: Shu Xi, courtesy name Guangwei, was a man of Yuancheng in Yangping—descendant of Han heir tutor Shu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi, styled Guangwei, came from Yuancheng in Yangping and descended from Shu Guang, tutor to the Han heir.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，廣曾孫孟達避難，自東海徙居沙鹿山南，因去疏之足，遂改姓焉。

translations.literal: At Wang Mang's end Guang's great-grandson Mengda fled turmoil, moved from Donghai to south of Mount Shalu, removed the foot radical from Shu and changed surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, Guang's descendant Mengda fled east to Mount Shalu and shortened the surname Shu by dropping its foot radical.

sentences.zh: 祖混，隴西太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hun was governor of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shu Hun governed Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父龕，馮翊太守，並有名譽。

translations.literal: His father Kan was governor of Fengyi—both had fame.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu Kan governed Fengyi—both father and grandfather were renowned.

sentences.zh: 晳博學多聞，與兄璆俱知名。

translations.literal: Xi was broadly learned; he and his elder brother Qiu were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi read widely; he and his brother Qiu shared fame.

sentences.zh: 少游國學，或問博士曹志曰：「當今好學者誰乎？

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the national academy; someone asked Erudite Cao Zhi: "Who today loves learning?"
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial academy someone asked Erudite Cao Zhi who still truly studied.

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「陽平束廣微好學不倦，人莫及也。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Shu Guangwei of Yangping loves learning tirelessly—none can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi named Shu Guangwei of Yangping as tireless—peerless among scholars.

sentences.zh: 」還鄉里，察孝廉，舉茂才，皆不就。

translations.literal: Returning home he was inspected Filial and nominated Flourishing Talent—both without rising.
translations.idiomatic: Home callers nominated him Filial and Flourishing Talent—he declined both.

sentences.zh: 璆娶石鑒從女，棄之，鑒以為憾，諷州郡公府不得辟，故晳等久不得調。

translations.literal: Qiu married a niece of Shi Jian's cousin but divorced her; Jian bore resentment and hinted that commanderies and senior offices must not summon him—therefore Xi and others long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His brother divorced Shi Jian's niece; Shi Jian blocked both brothers from office until grudges faded.

sentences.zh: 太康中，郡界大旱，晳為邑人請雨，三日而雨注，眾謂晳誠感，為作歌曰：「束先生，通神明，請天三日甘雨零。

translations.literal: During Taikang a great drought struck the commandery; Xi prayed for rain on behalf of townsfolk—on the third day torrential rain fell; crowds deemed Xi's sincerity had moved heaven and composed a song: "Master Shu penetrates spirit luminaries; begging heaven three days sweet rain sprinkles."
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang's drought he prayed for his neighbors and rain burst forth on day three—locals sang that Master Shu moved heaven.

sentences.zh: 我黍以育，我稷以生。

translations.literal: Our millet thereby grows; our glutinous millet thereby lives.
translations.idiomatic: Our sorghum grows; our millet thrives.

sentences.zh: 何以疇之？

translations.literal: How shall we repay him?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we repay him?

sentences.zh: 報束長生。

translations.literal: We repay Master Changsheng.
translations.idiomatic: We repay Master Changsheng.

sentences.zh: 」晳與衛恆厚善，聞恆遇禍，自本郡赴喪。

translations.literal: Xi was thick as friends with Wei Heng; hearing Heng met disaster he hurried from his commandery to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Close to Wei Heng, he raced from home to mourn Heng's murder.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《勸農》及《餅》諸賦，文頗鄙俗，時人薄之。

translations.literal: He once composed fu such as Encourage Agriculture and Cakes—the language rather vulgar; people of the time slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: His fu on farming and cakes sounded coarse—contemporaries sneered.

sentences.zh: 而性沈退，不慕榮利，作《玄居釋》以擬《客難》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yet his nature was retiring—he did not covet glory or profit; he composed Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery modeled on Guest's Difficulty, its text saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spurned rank and fashioned his Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery after the Guest's Difficulty:

sentences.zh: 束晳閒居，門人並侍。

translations.literal: Shu Xi dwelt in leisure—disciples stood attendance together.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi lived in quiet retirement surrounded by disciples.

sentences.zh: 方下帷深譚，隱-{几}-而咍，含毫散藻，考撰同異，在側者進而問之曰：「蓋聞道尚變通，達者無窮。

translations.literal: Drawing the curtain for deep talk, leaning on the armrest while smiling, holding brush-tip to scatter brilliance, collating similarities and differences—those beside advanced and asked: "We have heard the Way esteems adaptability; the attained know no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Behind lowered curtains he leaned on the armrest, brush in hand, collating texts until disciples pressed him: they said true doctrine bends with events—masters face no ceiling.

sentences.zh: 世亂則救其紛，時泰則扶其隆。

translations.literal: Age chaotic—then rescue its tangles; age tranquil—then uphold its prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue chaos when the age tangles; uphold greatness when peace reigns.

sentences.zh: 振天維以贊百務，熙帝載而鼓皇風。

translations.literal: Raise heaven's net to aid the myriad tasks; brighten the emperor's record and drum royal winds.
translations.idiomatic: Hold up heaven's warp for every task; brighten the monarch's merit and fan imperial virtue abroad.

sentences.zh: 生則率土樂其存，死則宇內哀其終。

translations.literal: Living, then all within the soil rejoices in his existence; dying, then within the seas they mourn his end.
translations.idiomatic: Alive, the realm rejoices with him; dead, every shore mourns.

sentences.zh: 是以君子屈己伸道，不恥幹時。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen bend themselves to extend the Way, not ashamed to pursue timely employment.
translations.idiomatic: So worthies bend pride to advance the Way and seize office without shame.

sentences.zh: 上國有不索何獲之言，《周易》著躍以求進之辭。

translations.literal: The Central States have the saying "nothing sought, nothing gained"; the Changes marks leaping to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland says seek or starve; the Zhou yi praises those who leap toward duty.

sentences.zh: 莘老負金鉉以陳烹割之說，齊客當康衢而詠《白水》之詩。

translations.literal: Old Shen shouldered bronze tripods expounding butcher-kings; the Qi traveler sang White Water on the broad avenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's cook preached over cauldrons; a Qi pilgrim sang White Water in the highway.

sentences.zh: 今先生耽道修藝，嶷然山峙，潛朗通微，洽覽深識，夜兼忘寐之勤，晝騁鑽玄之思，曠年累稔，不墮其志。

translations.literal: Now, sir, you steep yourself in the Way and cultivate arts—towering like a mountain, latent brilliance penetrating subtlety, browsing deeply and knowing broadly—by night forgetting sleep's toil, by day racing after arcane thought—year piled on year without abandoning your resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you bury yourself in learning like a silent peak—years of sleepless reading—never yielding.

sentences.zh: 鱗翼成而愈伏，術業優而不試。

translations.literal: Yet scales and wings fully formed you hide still deeper; arts perfected yet never tested.
translations.idiomatic: Fully fledged, you burrow deeper; mastery ripe, you refuse trial.

sentences.zh: 乃欲闔櫝辭價，泥蟠深處，永戢琳琅之耀，匿首窮魚之渚，當唐年而慕長沮，邦有道而反甯武。

translations.literal: You would shut the coffer and decline valuation, coil like mud in deep recesses, forever sheathing gleaming jade, hiding your head on islets where stranded fish dwell—when Tang reigns you envy Chang Ju; when the state has the Way you imitate Ning Wu.
translations.idiomatic: You would bury treasure like fish in drying pools—longing for Chang Ju even under Tang's golden rule.

sentences.zh: 識彼迷此，愚竊不取。

translations.literal: Seeing them lost yet holding this course—in my foolishness I dare not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring their folly wins no praise from me.

sentences.zh: 若乃士以援登，進必待求，附勢之黨橫擢，則林藪之彥不抽，丹墀步紈誇之童，東野遺白顛之叟。

translations.literal: Moreover scholars climb through patronage—advancement awaits solicitation; when factions of opportunists seize posts unchecked, forest worthies cannot emerge; silk-shod boys swagger on vermilion steps while white-haired elders linger east of town.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars rise through patrons—when climbers glut court, hermits starve while silk youths parade and gray scholars rot outside.

sentences.zh: 盍亦因數都而事博陸，憑鷁首以涉洪流，蹈翠雲以駭逸龍，振光耀以驚沈鰌。

translations.literal: Why not seize season and emulate Lu's minister, ride kingfisher prow across vast currents, tread emerald clouds to startle soaring dragons, shake radiance to alarm sunk fish?
translations.idiomatic: Better borrow Bo Lu's tide—rise on floods and startle dragons.

sentences.zh: 徒屈蟠于陷井，眄天路而不遊，學既積而身困，夫何為乎秘丘。

translations.literal: Content to coil in a pit gazing at heaven's road yet never roaming—learning piles while the body languishes—what use hiding on secret hills?
translations.idiomatic: Why lie in wells studying heaven yet waste away?

sentences.zh: 且歲不我與，時若奔駟，有來無反，難得易失。

translations.literal: Moreover years do not wait on us; seasons gallop like swift horses—what comes does not return; hard to gain, easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Years gallop—gain once, lose forever.

sentences.zh: 先生不知盱豫之讖悔遲，而忘夫朋盍之義務疾，亦豈能登海湄而抑東流之水，臨虞泉而招西歸之日？

translations.literal: Sir, do you not know hesitation's regret arrives late while forgetting fellowship demands haste—can you climb the ocean verge and dam the eastern flood, stand by Yu's spring and beckon the western sun?
translations.idiomatic: Hesitation invites regret; no man dams east tides or recalls western sun.

sentences.zh: 徒以曲畏為梏，儒學自桎，囚大道於環堵，苦形骸於蓬室。

translations.literal: Only take twisted fear as fetters, Confucian study as self-shackles, imprison the great Way within a mud wall, torture your frame inside a thatched room.
translations.idiomatic: Do not chain the Way to hovel dread.

sentences.zh: 豈若托身權戚，憑勢假力，擇棲芳林，飛不待翼，夕宿七娥之房，朝享五鼎之食，匡三正則太階平，贊五教而玉繩直。

translations.literal: How compare lodging with powerful kin, borrowing influence to perch in fragrant woods—soaring needs no wings—sleep nights in towers of seven beauties, dine mornings on five-tripod feasts—support the three norms then the Grand Stairway levels; aid the five teachings then the Jade Cord hangs straight?
translations.idiomatic: Compare patronage—palace nights, tripod feasts—against fasting alone?

sentences.zh: 孰若茹藿餐蔬，終身自匿哉！」

translations.literal: How compare chewing greens and eating vegetable stalks, hiding life-long?"
translations.idiomatic: Or gnaw greens forever in hiding?"

sentences.zh: 束子曰：「居！

translations.literal: Master Shu said: "Sit!
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi answered: "Sit.

sentences.zh: 吾將導爾以君子之道，諭爾以出處之事。

translations.literal: I shall guide you in the gentleman's Way and instruct you in matters of withdrawal and emergence.
translations.idiomatic: Let me teach the gentleman's path of serving or hiding.

sentences.zh: 爾其明受餘訊，謹聽餘志。

translations.literal: You must clearly receive my inquiry and heedfully listen to my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hear me out carefully.

sentences.zh: 昔元一既啟，兩儀肇立，離光夜隱，望舒晝戢，羽族翔林，蟩蛁赴濕，物從性之所安，士樂志之所執，或背豐榮以岩棲，或排蘭闥而求入，在野者龍逸，在朝者鳳集。

translations.literal: When primordial unity opened, the two modes began—lunar radiance hid by night, moon chariot rested by day; feathered kin soar forests, crawling things hurry to damp—things follow nature's ease, gentlemen delight in mind's grasp—some turn from glory to cliff dwellings, some push through orchid gates to enter court—those in wilds hide like dragons; those at court gather like phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Since chaos split into yin and yang, creatures and sages alike seek fit dwelling—some flee court, some embrace it.

sentences.zh: 雖其軌跡不同，而道無貴賤，必安其業，交不相羨，稷、契奮庸以宣道，巢、由洗耳以避禪，同垂不朽之稱，俱入賢者之流。

translations.literal: Although their tracks differ, the Way knows no noble or base—each settles his task, envying not the other; Ji and Qi strove in office to broadcast the Way; Chao and Xu washed ears to flee abdication—both earn immortality's name and enter the stream of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Office and reclusion differ outwardly yet share worth—Yi Yin and Duke Ji served; Chao Fu and Xu You fled—and both became paragons.

sentences.zh: 參名比譽，誰劣誰優？

translations.literal: Set names side by side—who proves inferior, who superior?
translations.idiomatic: Compare them fairly—who falls short?

sentences.zh: 何必貪與二八為群，而恥為七人之疇乎！

translations.literal: Why must you crave joining the Eightfold bands yet feel shame matching the Seven Worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Why envy the Eight Neighbors yet scorn the Seven Sages?

sentences.zh: 且道睽而通，士不同趣，吾竊綴處者之末行，未敢聞子之高喻，將忽蒲輪而不眄，夫何權戚之雲附哉！

translations.literal: Moreover when ways diverge yet communicate, scholars pursue unlike aims—I merely stitch myself to the recluse's tail—I dare not hear your lofty metaphor—shall I ignore the herb wagon and never glance—what talk of attaching to powerful kin?
translations.idiomatic: Paths fork—call me late hermit if you will—I ignore wagons of summons and scorn power brokers.

sentences.zh: 昔周、漢中衰，時難自托，福兆既開，患端亦作，朝游巍峨之宮，夕墜崢嶸之壑，晝笑夜歎，晨華暮落，忠不足以衛己，禍不可以預度，是士諱登朝而競赴林薄。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou and Han declined—hard times forced self-reliance—once fortune's gate opened, calamity's mouth opened too—morning roaming lofty palaces, evening plunged sheer ravines—laughing by day, sighing by night—bloom at dawn, drop by dusk—loyalty could not shield oneself; disaster could not be foreseen—therefore gentlemen shunned court and raced to woods.
translations.idiomatic: Late Zhou and Han taught that royal favor opens peril—morning minister, evening corpse—so wise men fled to forests.

sentences.zh: 或毀名自汙，或不食其祿，比從政於匣笥之龜，譬官者於郊廟之犢，公孫泣涕而辭相，楊雄抗論於赤族。
