translations.literal: Some ruined names with self-filth; some refused salaries—compare taking office to tortoise in a box; compare officials to calves at suburban altars—Gongsun wept declining minister; Yang Xiong argued though clan faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: Men smeared themselves or refused grain—office seemed boxed turtles or sacrificial calves—ministers wept or debated unto death.

sentences.zh: 今大晉熙隆，六合寧靜。

translations.literal: Now great Jin shines—the six harmonies tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Today Jin rules calm seas.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆止毒，熊羆輟猛，五刑勿用，八紘備整，主無驕肆之怒，臣無犛纓之請，上下相安，率禮從道。

translations.literal: Wasps halt poison; bears and brown bears cease fierceness—five punishments unused; eight cords prepared—lord bears no arrogant wrath; ministers seek no ox-haired pardon—high and low dwell secure; all observe ritual and follow the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons sleep; punishments idle—throne and ministers trust each other.

sentences.zh: 朝養觸邪之獸，庭有指佞之草，禍戮可以忠逃，寵祿可以順保。

translations.literal: Court nurtures truth-touching beasts; courtyard grows slander-pointing grass—execution flees the loyal; favor follows the tractable.
translations.idiomatic: Palace beasts sniff evil; magical grass marks flattery—loyalty earns life.

sentences.zh: 且夫進無險懼，而惟寂之務者，率其性也。

translations.literal: Moreover advancement harbors no cliff-edge fear—yet cleaving to silence alone follows native temperament.
translations.idiomatic: Risk-free promotion suits some temperaments.

sentences.zh: 兩可俱是，而舍彼趣此者，從其志也。

translations.literal: When both options fit yet one rejects this for that—follow heart's bent.
translations.idiomatic: When both paths serve, choose passion.

sentences.zh: 蓋無為可以解天下之紛，澹泊可以救國家之急，當位者事有所窮，陳策者言有不入，翟璜不能回西鄰之寇，平、勃不能正如意之立，幹木臥而秦師退，四皓起而戚姬泣。

translations.literal: Utter non-action untangles realm chaos; utter simplicity meets state emergencies—those enthroned reach impasses; advisers miss ears—Zhai Huang could not turn back western neighbors' raid; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not legitimize Prince Ruyi's installation—Duanmu Ke lay ill yet Qin armies withdrew; Four Hoary Heads rose and Lady Qi wept.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal can steady crises: Zhai Huang failed to stop western raids; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not place Liu Ruyi; yet Duanmu Ke merely stayed home and Qin fled; four graybeards emerged and Lady Qi wept fate.

sentences.zh: 夫如是何舍何執，何去何就？

translations.literal: Given this—what cling to, what adopt; what leave, what take?
translations.idiomatic: So what stays fixed?

sentences.zh: 謂山岑之林為芳，穀底之莽為臭。

translations.literal: They call mountaincrest woods fragrant and valley weeds rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain air smells sweet; swamps reek.

sentences.zh: 守分任性，唯天所授，鳥不假甲於龜，魚不借足於獸，何必笑孤竹之貧而羨齊景之富！

translations.literal: Guard allotment and follow nature—only heaven grants—birds borrow no armor from tortoises; fish borrow no feet from beasts—why mock lone bamboo's poverty and envy Qi Jing's wealth!
translations.idiomatic: Each creature uses heaven's gift—why mock the poor or envy kings?

sentences.zh: 恥布衣以肆志，甯文裘而拖繡。

translations.literal: Ashamed of plain cloth yet indulging will—better patched fur dragging embroidered train.
translations.idiomatic: Rather coarse robe with purpose than silk without.

sentences.zh: 且能約其躬，則儋石之畜以豐；

translations.literal: When able to restrain the person, then a peck of grain yields plenty;
translations.idiomatic: Restrain appetite—a peck fills you;

sentences.zh: 苟肆其欲，則海陵之積不足；

translations.literal: if unrestrained in desire, even Hailing granaries cannot suffice.
translations.idiomatic: indulge—Hailing stores empty.

sentences.zh: 存道德者，則匹夫之身可榮；

translations.literal: Preserve morality—then a commoner's body may shine;
translations.idiomatic: Virtue glorifies a commoner;

sentences.zh: 忘大倫者，則萬乘之主猶辱。

translations.literal: forget great relations—even a lord of ten thousand chariots remains disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: sin disgraces emperors.

sentences.zh: 將研六籍以訓世，守寂泊以鎮俗，偶鄭老於海隅，匹嚴叟於僻蜀。

translations.literal: I shall grind the six classics to instruct the age; keep silence and simplicity to steady custom—pair old Zheng by the sea; match Yan Jun in Shu wilds.
translations.idiomatic: I study the six classics to teach the world; couple Zheng on the coast with Yan in Shu.

sentences.zh: 且世乙太虛為輿，玄爐為肆，神游莫競之林，心存無營之室，榮利不擾其覺，殷憂不幹其寐，捐誇者之所貪，收躁務之所棄，雉聖籍之荒蕪，總群言之一至。

translations.literal: Moreover taking Great Void as carriage, dark furnace as market—spirit roams trackless groves; mind lodges desireless chamber—glory does not disturb waking; deep grief does not touch sleep—discard what boasters crave; gather what bustle discards—order sage texts' wasteland; gather myriad tongues to one arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Ride emptiness as cart; wander mind in silent rooms—spurn fame's trash; harvest truth's scraps.

sentences.zh: 全素履於丘園，背纓緌而長逸，請子課吾業於千載，無聽吾言於今日也。」

translations.literal: Keep plain sandals in hill gardens; turn from cap tassels forever—ask me again after ages—heed me not today."
translations.idiomatic: Keep straw shoes in hills—judge me later—not today."

sentences.zh: 張華見而奇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua saw it and deemed him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua marveled at the piece.

sentences.zh: 石鑒卒，王戎乃辟璆。

translations.literal: When Shi Jian died, Wang Rong then summoned Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jian died Wang Rong finally called Shu Qiu.

sentences.zh: 華召晳為掾，又為司空、下邳王晃所辟。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua summoned Xi as clerk; also the Prince of Xiapi, Prince Huang, summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua took Shu Xi as aide; Prince Huang of Xiapi also summoned him.

sentences.zh: 華為司空，復以為賊曹屬。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua became Minister of Works he again made him bureau clerk for bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of works Zhang Hua appointed him bandit-suppression clerk.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣農，晳上議曰：轉佐著作郎，撰《晉書·帝紀》、十《志》，遷轉博士，著作如故。

translations.literal: The court wished to expand agriculture; Xi submitted a memorial saying: he was transferred to assist as Editorial Director, compiled the Jin shu annals and the ten treatises, advanced to erudite while still composing.
translations.idiomatic: When the state sought wider farming, his memorial led to posts as assistant editorial director, compiler of the Jin annals and monographs, and finally doctorate while continuing to write.

sentences.zh: 初，，汲郡人不准盜發魏襄王墓，或言安釐王塚，得竹書數十車。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man of Ji commandery named Bu Zhan broke into the tomb of King Xiang of Wei—some say it was King Axi's tomb—obtaining several cartloads of bamboo documents.
translations.idiomatic: Grave robber Bu Zhan in Ji opened King Xiang of Wei's tomb, reportedly King Axi's, and hauled out bamboo-text carts.

sentences.zh: 其《紀年》十三篇，記夏以來至周幽王為犬戎所滅，以事接之，三家分，仍述魏事至安釐王之二十年。

translations.literal: Its Annals in thirteen scrolls record from Xia down to King You of Zhou destroyed by the Quan Rong, then links events to the three families' partition, still narrating Wei affairs to the twentieth year of King Axi.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen-scroll Bamboo Annals run from Xia through Western Zhou's fall, then carry Wei down to 299 BCE.

sentences.zh: 蓋魏國之史書，大略與《春秋》皆多相應。

translations.literal: In general Wei state's history largely corresponds with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei annals align broadly with the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 其中經傳大異，則雲夏年多殷；

translations.literal: Where its classics and commentaries differ greatly, it says the Xia calendar had more years than Yin's;
translations.idiomatic: It claims Xia recorded more years than Shang;

sentences.zh: 益幹啟位，啟殺之；

translations.literal: Yi usurped Qi's place; Qi killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Yi seized Qi's throne and Qi killed him;

sentences.zh: 太甲殺伊尹；

translations.literal: Tai Jia killed Yi Yin;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia executed Yi Yin;

sentences.zh: 文丁殺季曆；

translations.literal: Wen Ding killed Ji Li;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ding killed Ji Li;

sentences.zh: 自周受命，至穆王百年，非穆王壽百歲也；

translations.literal: from Zhou receiving the mandate to King Mu was one hundred years—it does not mean King Mu lived one hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: A century from Zhou's Mandate to Mu does not mean King Mu reached one hundred;

sentences.zh: 幽王既亡，有共伯和者攝行天子事，非二相共和也。

translations.literal: after You perished, one Duke He of Gong acted as Son of Heaven—it is not the two ministers' joint regency.
translations.idiomatic: After King You fell, the Earl of Gong named He ruled as regent—not the joint stewardship of two Zhou ministers that later gloss became "harmony."

sentences.zh: 其《易經》二篇，與《周易》上下經同。

translations.literal: Its Changes in two scrolls match the Zhou yi upper and lower classics.
translations.idiomatic: The two scrolls of Changes match the received Zhou yi hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 《易繇陰陽卦》二篇，與《周易》略同，《繇辭》則異。

translations.literal: Changes' Hexagram Stems Yin and Yang in two scrolls resemble the Zhou yi though the line texts differ.
translations.idiomatic: The yin-yang line scrolls echo the Zhou yi with variant line statements.

sentences.zh: 《卦下易經》一篇，似《說卦》而異。

translations.literal: Changes under the hexagrams in one scroll resembles Shuo Gua with differences.
translations.idiomatic: A single scroll of sub-hexagram Changes resembles the Shuo Gua with differences.

sentences.zh: 《公孫段》二篇，公孫段與邵陟論《易》。

translations.literal: Gong Sun Duan in two scrolls—Duan and Shao Zhi discuss the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls on Gongsun Duan debate the Changes with Shao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 《國語》三篇，言楚、晉事。

translations.literal: Guo yu in three scrolls—speaks of Chu and Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls of state conversations cover Chu and Jin.

sentences.zh: 《名》三篇，似《禮記》，又似《爾雅》《論語》。

translations.literal: Ming in three scrolls—resemble the Record of Rites, also the Erya and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls of "Names" read like the Record of Rites, Erya, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 《師春》一篇，書《左傳》諸卜筮，「師春」似是造書者姓名也。

translations.literal: Spring Master in one scroll—records the Zuo zhuan's divinations; "Master Spring" may be the compiler's name.
translations.idiomatic: The "Shi Chun" scroll lists Zuo divinations; the title may record an author's name.

sentences.zh: 《瑣語》十一篇，諸國卜夢妖怪相書也。

translations.literal: Suo yu in eleven scrolls—various states' dream and omen divinations.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven scrolls of petty talk collect omens and dreams from many states.

sentences.zh: 《梁丘藏》一篇，先敘魏之世數，次言丘藏金玉事。

translations.literal: Liangqiu Zang in one scroll—first traces Wei reign-counts, then speaks of hill treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangqiu Zang scroll counts Wei generations then catalogs buried treasure.

sentences.zh: 《繳書》二篇，論弋射法。

translations.literal: Jiao shu in two scrolls—discuss archery methods.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls on knot-shooting arts.

sentences.zh: 《生封》一篇，帝王所封。

translations.literal: Sheng Feng in one scroll—records kings' enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: One scroll of living enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 《大曆》二篇，鄒子談天類也。

translations.literal: Great Calendar in two scrolls—like Zou Yan's celestial discussions.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls of macro-calendars akin to Zou Yan's astronomy.

sentences.zh: 《穆天子傳》五篇，言周穆王遊行四海，見帝台、西王母。

translations.literal: Mu Tianzi zhuan in five scrolls—relates King Mu of Zhou touring seas and meeting Xi Wangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Five scrolls of King Mu's travels among seas and holy peaks.

sentences.zh: 《圖詩》一篇，畫贊之屬也。

translations.literal: Diagram Poems in one scroll—belongs with inscribed praises.
translations.idiomatic: One scroll of picture poems like engraved encomia.

sentences.zh: 又雜書十九篇：《周食田法》，《周書》，《論楚事》，《周穆王美人盛姬死事》。

translations.literal: Plus nineteen miscellaneous scrolls: Zhou Food-Field Law, Zhou Documents, Discourse on Chu, King Mu's Beauty Sheng Ji Dies.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen more fragments cover Zhou land law, Chu debates, and Lady Sheng Ji's death.

sentences.zh: 大凡七十五篇，七篇簡書折壞，不識名題。

translations.literal: Altogether seventy-five scrolls; seven bamboo bundles snapped beyond reading titles.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five pieces survived; seven bundles shattered unreadable.

sentences.zh: 塚中又得銅劍一枚，長二尺五寸。

translations.literal: They also recovered one bronze sword two chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: One bronze sword measured two and a half feet.

sentences.zh: 漆書皆科斗字。

translations.literal: All lacquer writing used tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: Every lacquer text showed tadpole seal forms.

sentences.zh: 初發塚者燒策照取寶物，及官收之，多燼簡斷劄，文既殘缺，不復詮次。

translations.literal: First diggers burned slips seeking jewels; when officials reclaimed them, many slips charred and snapped—the writing ruined beyond collation.
translations.idiomatic: Looters burned bundles for treasure; imperial clerks found charred scraps impossible to order.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其書付秘書校綴次第，尋考指歸，而以今文寫之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu handed them to the palace library to splice order and rewrite into contemporary script.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu tasked the secretariat to reorder and transcribe into clerical script.

sentences.zh: 晳在著作，得觀竹書，隨疑分釋，皆有義證。

translations.literal: Xi served as compiler and inspected the bamboo texts— whenever doubts arose he partitioned explanations with proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Editing at the palace, Shu Xi glossed every doubtful passage.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問摯虞三日曲水之義，虞對曰：「漢章帝時，平原徐肇以三月初生三女，至三日俱亡，村人以為怪，乃招攜之水濱洗祓，遂因水以泛觴，其義起此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu the meaning of the third-day winding-water banquet; Yu replied: "Under Han Zhangdi plaindweller Xu Zhao bore three daughters on the third day of the third month—all died that day; villagers thought it odd and gathered riverside to wash away ill luck and floated cups—thus began the custom."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked about the worm-water festival; Zhi Yu traced it to a Han village tragedy washing omens at the river.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必如所談，便非好事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If truly as you tell, it was no happy affair."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called that origin ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 」晳進曰：「虞小生，不足以知，臣請言之。

translations.literal: Xi advanced saying: "Yu is young—cannot know fully—allow your servant to explain."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi interrupted: Zhi Yu was too junior—the fuller answer follows.

sentences.zh: 昔周公成洛邑，因流水以泛酒，故逸詩云『羽觴隨波』。

translations.literal: Ancient Duke Zhou completed Luoyi and floated wine along flowing water—thus stray poems say 'cup feathers drift with waves.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhou floated cups when founding Luoyang—matching lost poems.

sentences.zh: 又秦昭王以三日置酒河曲，見金人奉水心之劍，曰：『令君制有西夏。

translations.literal: Further King Zhaoxiang of Qin feasted by the river bend on the third day and saw a golden man present a sword from water's heart, saying 'your lordship shall rule Western Xia.'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin held a third-day river banquet and dreamed river gods gifting swords.

sentences.zh: 』乃霸諸侯，因此立為曲水。

translations.literal: then he rose among feudal lords—therefore established winding-water rites.
translations.idiomatic: That feast founded the winding-water ritual.

sentences.zh: 二漢相緣，皆為盛集。

translations.literal: Both Han dynasties continued it—all splendid gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han kept the tradition as grand festivals.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，賜晳金五十斤。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced greatly and awarded Xi fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he gave Shu Xi fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 時有人于嵩高山下得竹簡一枚，上兩行科斗書，傳以相示，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Once someone found beneath Song Mountain a bamboo slip with two columns of tadpole script—shown around, nobody could read it.
translations.idiomatic: Hikers at Songshan found tadpole-writing slips nobody could decipher.

sentences.zh: 司空張華以問晳，晳曰：「此漢明帝顯節陵中策文也。

translations.literal: Director Zhang Hua showed Shu Xi who said: "This is Eulogy Script from Emperor Ming's Xianjie tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua consulted Shu Xi who identified Han Mingdi tomb tally script.

sentences.zh: 」檢驗果然，時人伏其博識。

translations.literal: Inspection proved him right—people admired his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Checks proved him right—scholars hailed his learning.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，請為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun as minister of state invited him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun summoned him private secretary.

sentences.zh: 晳辭疾罷歸，教授門徒。

translations.literal: Xi pleaded illness, resigned home, taught disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi pleaded sickness, retired to teach.

sentences.zh: 年四十卒，元城市裏為之廢業，門生故人立碑墓側。

translations.literal: He died at forty—the Yuan marketplace halted trade; disciples and friends raised a stele beside his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His death at forty closed Yuan markets; friends carved his monument.

sentences.zh: 晳才學博通，所著《三魏人士傳》，《七代通記》、《晉書·紀》、《志》，遇亂亡失。

translations.literal: Xi's learning embraced everything—his Records of Wei Worthies, Seven-Dynasty Comprehensive Records, and Jin annals perished in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: War swallowed his Wei roster and Jin drafts.

sentences.zh: 其《五經通論》、《發蒙記》、《補亡詩》、文集數十篇，行於世雲。

translations.literal: Yet his Five Classics Comprehensive Discussion, Enlightenment Notes, Supplementary Lost Poems, and collected writings dozens of scrolls still circulated.
translations.idiomatic: His Five Classics synthesis, primer, supplement poems, and essays survived in tens of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 王接

translations.literal: Wang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Wang Jie.

sentences.zh: 王接，字祖遊，河東猗氏人，漢京兆尹尊十世孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, courtesy name Zuyou, was a man of Yishi in Hedong—tenth-generation descendant of Han metropolitan governor Wang Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, styled Zuyou, came from Yishi in Hedong—descended from Han Governor Wang Zun.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，世修儒史之學。

translations.literal: His father Wei perpetuated Confucian historiography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Wei taught classics and history.

sentences.zh: 魏中領軍曹羲作《至公論》，蔚善之，而著《至機論》，辭義甚美。

translations.literal: Wei central commander Cao Xi wrote On Perfect Impartiality which Wei praised—Wei wrote On Ultimate Pivot with exquisite argument.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xi's essay inspired Wang Wei's counterpiece.

sentences.zh: 官至夏陽侯相。

translations.literal: He rose to magistrate of Xiayang marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: He became Xiayang county administrator.

sentences.zh: 接幼喪父，哀毀過禮，鄉親皆歎曰：「王氏有子哉！

translations.literal: Jie lost his father young—grief exceeded ritual—neighbors sighed: "Wang clan has a worthy son!"
translations.idiomatic: Orphans mourning beyond propriety moved the hamlet.

sentences.zh: 」渤海劉原為河東太守，好奇，以旌才為務。

translations.literal: Bohai Liu Yuan governed Hedong and loved the unusual—seeking talent was his task.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan of Bohai loved prodigies.

sentences.zh: 同郡馮收試經為郎，七十餘，薦接于原曰：「夫驊騮不總轡，則非造父之肆；

translations.literal: Townmate Feng Shou tested classics and became gentleman cadet past seventy—recommended Jie to Yuan: "A fine steed without reins never reaches Zaofu's stable;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shou likened Jie to an unbridled thoroughbred;

sentences.zh: 明月不流光，則非隋侯之掌。

translations.literal: bright moon without flowing light never rests in Suihou's palm."
translations.idiomatic: hidden gems need patrons.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明府苞黃中之德，耀重離之明，求賢與能，小無遺錯，是以鄙老思獻所知。

translations.literal: I humbly consider Your Honor harbors yellow-center virtue and doubled-li brilliance—seeking worth without missing trifles—so this old man wishes to offer what he knows.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Liu Yuan to hire Wang Jie.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士王接，岐嶷俊異，十三而孤，居喪盡禮，學過目而知，義觸類而長，斯玉鉉之妙味，經世之徽猷也。

translations.literal: I have noted recluse Wang Jie—precocious and singular—orphaned at thirteen—mourning fulfilled ritual—learning grasped at sight—principles extend by analogy—such is jade-handle savor and guiding-world subtle plan.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Jie's orphan brilliance.

sentences.zh: 不患玄黎之不啟，竊樂春英之及時。

translations.literal: Not fearing dark dawn's delay—I rejoice spring blossoms arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: He urged timely promotion.

sentences.zh: 」原即禮命，接不受。

translations.literal: Yuan immediately summoned with ritual—Jie declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan invited him—Jie refused.

sentences.zh: 原乃呼見曰：「君欲慕肥遁之高邪？

translations.literal: Yuan then summoned him saying: "Do you emulate lofty reclusion?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu asked if he mimicked hermits.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「接薄祜，少孤而無兄弟，母老疾篤，故無心為吏。

translations.literal: He replied: "Jie suffers thin fortune—orphaned without brothers—mother aged and critically ill—therefore no heart for clerking."
translations.idiomatic: Jie cited sick mother.

sentences.zh: 」及母終，柴毀骨立，居墓次積年，備覽眾書，多出異義。

translations.literal: When mother died he wasted to bones beside her tomb for years—reading every book—often dissenting received glosses.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he lived by the mound emaciated, disputing classical readings.

sentences.zh: 性簡率，不修俗操，鄉里大族多不能善之，唯裴頠雅知焉。

translations.literal: Nature frank and blunt—cared not for vulgar conduct—great local clans mostly disliked him—only Pei Yi truly understood.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt honesty offended magnates; only Pei Yi befriended him.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守柳澹、散騎侍郎裴遐、尚書僕射鄧攸皆與接友善。

translations.literal: Pingyang governor Liu Dan, cavalier attendant Pei Xia, minister Deng You were all friends.
translations.idiomatic: Officials Liu Dan, Pei Xia, and Deng You befriended him.

sentences.zh: 後為郡主簿，迎太守溫宇，宇奇之，轉功曹史。

translations.literal: Later he became county chief clerk—welcoming governor Wen Yu—Yu marveled and transferred him merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk to Governor Wen Yu he earned promotion.

sentences.zh: 州辟部平陽從事。

translations.literal: The province summoned him Pingyang staff.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial office took him on.

sentences.zh: 時泰山羊亮為平陽太守，薦之于司隸校尉王堪，出補都官從事。

translations.literal: When Taishan Yang Liang governed Pingyang he recommended Jie to metropolitan commandant Wang Kan—appointed capital surveillance aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang forwarded him to Wang Kan.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning he was nominated Flourishing Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning brought his Flourishing Talent nomination.

sentences.zh: 友人滎陽潘滔遺接書曰：「摯虞、卞玄仁並謂足下應和鼎味，可無以應秀才行。

translations.literal: Friend Pan Tao wrote: "Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren both say you should harmonize cauldron flavors—do not reject Flourishing Talent without cause."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao pressed him to accept office.

sentences.zh: 」接報書曰：「今世道交喪，將遂剝亂，而識智之士鉗口韜筆，禍敗日深，如火之燎原，其可救乎？

translations.literal: Jie answered: "Now the Way totters toward stripping chaos—wise men seal lips—calamity deepens daily like spreading fire—how rescue?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied the age was burning—scholars stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 非榮斯行，欲極陳所見，冀有覺悟耳。

translations.literal: Not glory drives me—I wish to lay bare what I see hoping for awakening."
translations.idiomatic: He sought to wake the court.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，三王義舉，惠帝復阼，以國有大慶，天下秀孝一皆不試，接以為恨。

translations.literal: That year the three princes rose—Emperor Hui restored throne—because the state held great celebration all Flourishing Talent and Filial nominees skipped exams—Jie regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty skipped examinations—Jie resented missing his chance.

sentences.zh: 除中郎，補征虜將軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman cadet—supplemented marshal to the general who conquers barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He became aide to the northern expedition marshal.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，侍中嵇紹為亂兵所害，接議曰：「夫謀人之軍，軍敗則死之；

translations.literal: At the Battle of Dangyin when attendant Ji Shao fell to mutiny Jie argued: "One who plans another's army dies when it fails;
translations.idiomatic: After Ji Shao died at Dangyin, Jie invoked antiquity: whoever directs another's troops shares their fate.

sentences.zh: 謀人之國，國危則亡之，古之道也。

translations.literal: One who plots another's state perishes when it totters—such was antiquity's Way."
translations.idiomatic: Those who steer another man's throne answer with their lives when calamity comes—that maxim closed his plea.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，百官奔北，唯嵇紹守職以遇不道，可謂臣矣，又可稱痛矣。

translations.literal: At Dangyin the hundred officials fled—only Ji Shao kept post facing outrage—worthy minister—painfully admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Ji Shao's martyr loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今山東方欲大舉，宜明高節，以號令天下。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains prepares great campaign—we should proclaim lofty integrity to rally the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He urged honoring martyrs to inspire north China.

sentences.zh: 依《春秋》褒三累之義，加紹致命之賞，則遐邇向風，莫敢不肅矣。

translations.literal: Following Spring and Autumn's triple-tier praise—grant Ji Shao posthumous reward—then far and near will submit.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Spring and Autumn precedent for stacking honors.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Court accepted.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒欲遷駕長安，與關東乖異，以接成都王佐，難之，表轉臨汾公相國。

translations.literal: Prince Hejian Sima Yong wished to move the capital to Chang'an—estranged from east—assigning Jie aide to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying—Jie resisted—was transferred minister to Linjin duke.
translations.idiomatic: He resisted Yong's Chang'an move and earned transfer.

sentences.zh: 及東海王越率諸候討顒，尚書令王堪統行台，上請接補尚書殿中郎，未至而卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Prince Donghai Sima Yue led lords against Yong—minister Wang Kan commanded mobile headquarters—summoned Jie as palace gentleman—before arrival he died age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan summoned him but he died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 接學雖博通，特精《禮》《傳》。

translations.literal: Though Jie's learning vast he especially mastered Rites and Zuo commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in ritual and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 常謂《左氏》辭義贍富，自是一家書，不主為經發。

translations.literal: He often said Zuo's language rich—stands as its own book—not merely glossing classics.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zuo as independent history.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》附經立傳，經所不書，傳不妄起，于文為儉，通經為長。

translations.literal: Gongyang attaches to classics—classics silent means commentary silent—text economical yet penetrating classics superior.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred Gongyang's disciplined ties to the canon.

sentences.zh: 任城何休訓釋甚詳，而黜周王魯，大體乖硋，且志通《公羊》而往往還為《公羊》疾病。

translations.literal: Rencheng He Xiu's commentary thorough yet demotes Zhou and elevates Lu—great principle skewed—and though aiming at Gongyang often contradicts Gongyang itself.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized He Xiu's biases.

sentences.zh: 接乃更注《公羊春秋》，多有新義。

translations.literal: Jie therefore reannotated Gongyang Spring and Autumn with fresh interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote new Gongyang commentary.

sentences.zh: 時秘書丞衛恆考正汲塚書，未訖而遭難。

translations.literal: When secretary Cheng Wei Heng collated Ji tomb texts unfinished he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's Ji collation halted by death.

sentences.zh: 佐著作郎束皙述而成之，事多證異義。

translations.literal: Assistant compiler Shu Xi completed it—facts often diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi finished with disputed readings.

sentences.zh: 時東萊太守陳留王庭堅難之，亦有證據。

translations.literal: Then Donglai prefect Wang Tingjian of Chenliu challenged—also armed with proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingjian disputed both.

sentences.zh: 皙又釋難，而庭堅已亡。

translations.literal: Xi rebutted but Tingjian had died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi answered after Tingjian died.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎潘滔謂接曰：「卿才學理議，足解二子之紛，可試論之。

translations.literal: Cavalier attendant Pan Tao told Jie: "Your talent could settle both disputes—please adjudicate."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao asked Wang Jie to judge.

sentences.zh: 」接遂詳其得失。

translations.literal: Jie detailed their merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie weighed both sides.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、謝衡皆博物多聞，咸以為允當。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng—both encyclopedic—deemed his verdict fair.
translations.idiomatic: Experts approved.

sentences.zh: 又撰《列女後傳》七十二人，雜論議、詩賦、碑頌、駁難十餘萬言，喪亂盡失。

translations.literal: He also compiled Later Biographies of Exemplary Women seventy-two figures plus essays, fu, inscriptions, debates exceeding hundred thousand graphs—all lost to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His sequel on exemplary women and other essays burned in war.

sentences.zh: 長子愆期，流寓江南，緣父本意，更注《公羊》，又集《列女後傳》云。

translations.literal: Eldest son Yanqi fled south—following father's intent reannotated Gongyang and reassembled women's sequel.
translations.idiomatic: His son carried on Gongyang work in exile.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historical appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section: historians' verdict.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：皇甫謐素履幽貞，閒居養疾，留情筆削，敦悅丘墳，軒冕未足為榮，貧賤不以為恥，確乎不拔，斯固有晉之高人者歟！

translations.literal: Historians say: Huangfu Mi walked plain virtue in seclusion—nursed illness at leisure—devoted heart to brush-cutting—delighted in tomb texts—carriage caps could not tempt him—poverty brought no shame—firmly unmoved—surely Jin's lofty men!
translations.idiomatic: The editors praise Huangfu Mi as Jin's supreme recluse scholar.

sentences.zh: 洎乎《篤終》立論，薄葬昭儉，既戒奢于季氏，亦無取于王孫，可謂達存亡之機矣。

translations.literal: Down to writing Steadfast to the End advocating thin burial—warning extravagance like Jisun yet avoiding Wangsun Qing's extreme—he grasped life and death's hinge.
translations.idiomatic: They commend his funeral essay balancing thrift.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、束皙等並詳覽載籍，多識舊章，奏議可觀，文詞雅贍，可謂博聞之士也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, Shu Xi, and others examined transmitted writings in detail—well versed in old statutes—their memorials reward reading; phrasing refined and ample—may be called gentlemen of broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Shu Xi mastered classical precedent—eloquent memorialists rightly famed as polymaths.

sentences.zh: 或攝官延閣，裁成言事之書；

translations.literal: Some held provisional posts in the palace extension pavilion—edited directive writings on policy.
translations.idiomatic: Some staffed the imperial library and drafted state papers.

sentences.zh: 或蒞政秩宗，參定禋郊之禮。

translations.literal: Some governed as ministers of rites—jointly settled suburban sacrifice ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Others directed worship and fixed suburban ritual.

sentences.zh: 虞既厄於從理，皙乃年位不充，天之報施，何其爽也！

translations.literal: Yu suffered obstruction by circumstance—Xi never enjoyed rank matching his years—how uneven heaven's rewards!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu died thwarted; Shu Xi died young—heaven seemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 王接才調秀出，見賞知音，惜其夭枉，未申驥足，嗟夫！

translations.literal: Wang Jie's talents towered—recognized by discerning patrons—pitiful his premature cut-off never stretched swift stallions—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie won admirers yet died before his prime.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士安好逸，棲心蓬蓽。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Gentleman Mi loved ease—nested heart in brush-thatched hut.
translations.idiomatic: Verse praise: Huangfu Mi sought calm in a humble hut.

sentences.zh: 屬意文雅，忘懷榮秩。

translations.literal: Intent fixed on literary elegance—forgetting glory of office.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished care on letters and forgot titles.

sentences.zh: 遺制可稱，養生乖術。

translations.literal: Testament writings worthy—yet nurturing life misguided arts.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral tract shines though regimen proved fatal.

sentences.zh: 摯虞博聞，廣微絕群。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu broadly learned—Guangwei unmatched among peers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu was encyclopedic; Shu Guangwei stood apart.

sentences.zh: 財成禮度，刊緝遺文。

translations.literal: Completed ritual norms—edited surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: They framed ritual and collated relic texts.

sentences.zh: 魏篇式序，漢冊斯分。

translations.literal: Wei bamboo texts ordered—Han registers thereby distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They sequenced Wei slips and sorted Han archives.

sentences.zh: 祖遊後出，亦播清芬。
